===== CLAUDE.md =====

# Pico GTM Brain, agent entry point

This repository is the Pico go-to-market: two standalone GTMs, one for Shopify merchants and one for the implementers who set up their stores. You are an AI agent working inside it. Read this file, then follow its pointers. Do not improvise strategy the brain already settles.

## Read before any customer-facing output
1. `context/Pico_GTM_Master_Context.md`, the full strategy for both audiences. Source of truth. Read Section 0 and `status_notes` first.
2. `rules/glossary.md`, the canonical names and the distinctions that must never blur.
3. `rules/feature-status.md`, shipped versus in build. Check every capability you mention.
4. `rules/do-not-say.md`, forbidden claims and their safe replacements.
5. `rules/writing-rules.md`, mechanics, tone, channel discipline, signature lines.

Shortcut: `python3 tools/brain.py context <task> --audience <a>` prints the exact load set for a task. The MCP server in `tools/mcp_server.py` exposes the same through `brain_load_set`.

## This GTM is self-serve and pre-launch
Merchants: Shopify App Store, content and search including AI answer engines, and the product-led lifecycle. Load `reference/app-store-engine.md` first. Implementers: cold email to US recipients, LinkedIn messages sent by hand, and Upwork and Fiverr job posts for paid usability sessions. Load `reference/outreach-engine.md` first.

Out, refuse and redirect: paid ads, cold outbound to store owners, GCC or Arabic-market assets, LinkedIn automation or ads, any partner pitch inside Upwork or Fiverr, cold email to UK sole traders or the EU.

## Pick the audience first
Two audiences with separate value propositions. Never blend them in one asset.
- **Merchants:** US Shopify stores whose shoppers need help choosing. `reference/value-proposition-merchants.md`.
- **Implementers:** agencies, developers, theme developers, and freelancers. `reference/value-proposition-implementers.md`.

## Non-negotiables
- No revenue, sales, conversion, ROI, or lift claim. Pico measures what shoppers asked, saw, clicked, and added to cart.
- No invented proof: no install, review, or merchant count, no testimonial, no named merchant. The proof log is empty. Use open proof.
- No unshipped capability in the present tense. IN BUILD gets "coming soon" in the same sentence.
- Stock is "as of your last catalog sync". No semantic search, no checkout in chat.
- Never disparage Shopify or its tools. No named competitor comparison in copy that customers see.
- Partner terms only as published, and only from week 6: 25% for 24 months, 30% for lead partners, 10% managed.
- No em dashes. None of the banned words in `rules/writing-rules.md`.

## Before you ship
Run `python3 tools/brain.py lint <file>`, then walk `ops/QA-checklist.md`. State the audience, stage, and every capability's status flag.

## When something changes
New market input goes to `ops/signal-log.md` first (`python3 tools/brain.py signal ...`). Activity goes to the event log (`python3 tools/brain.py event ...`). A rule change follows the amendment procedure: the `rules/` ledger, then the master context, then `ops/decisions.md`, then the copy, then `python3 tools/brain.py build`. Never the other way around.

For BUILD, UPDATE, or OPERATE method, the installed skill is at `.claude/skills/go-to-market-brain/SKILL.md`.

# Pico Go-To-Market Master Context

This file distills two complete go-to-markets for Pico into one read: one for Shopify merchants, one for the implementers who set up Shopify stores. It exists so that any agent can execute Pico go-to-market work precisely without re-deriving strategy.

If you are an AI agent, read Section 0 first.

---

## 0. Agent operating instructions

**What this file is.** The distilled output of nine dashboards per audience (feature matrix, competitive analysis, positioning, ICP, buying committee, value proposition, customer journey, assets library, pricing), two lead magnets, two deck outlines, a 56-entry decision log, and a research pass dated 2026-11-03. Sources are listed in `ops/asset-index.md`. Every section is authoritative unless a status flag says otherwise.

**How to use it.**

1. Before any customer-facing copy, load the four files in `rules/`. They govern names, status, claims, and mechanics, and they override older phrasing you may pattern-match to.
2. Pick one audience: merchants or implementers. Never blend them in one asset.
3. Write to the funnel stage (Section 13). Do not sell past the stage.
4. Obey the strategic verdicts (Section 9). Do not contradict them, and do not describe a decided direction as shipped.
5. Use `ops/copy-bank.md` verbatim where a line exists. Run `ops/QA-checklist.md` before returning anything.

**Hard guardrails, never violate:**

- No revenue, sales, conversion, ROI, or lift claim about Pico or about a client's results. Pico measures what shoppers asked, saw, clicked, and added to cart.
- No invented proof. No install count, review count, rating, testimonial, named merchant, or metric. The customer proof log is empty.
- No unshipped capability in the present tense. Check `rules/feature-status.md` for every capability you mention.
- No disparaging Shopify or its tools, and no comparative claim about a named competitor in copy that customers see without a sourced, dated finding.
- No copy for an excluded channel (Section 14). Refuse and offer the in-scope channel.
- No em dashes, and none of the banned words in `rules/writing-rules.md`.

---

## 1. House writing rules

Short paragraphs, one to three sentences. Specific numbers, named capabilities, and checkable facts over adjectives. Commas or a restructure instead of em dashes. Banned words: leverage, unlock, seamless, robust, streamline, cutting-edge, empower, and their variants. The register is plain and exact, because merchants are wary of app bills and AI claims, and implementers carry the support burden of anything they recommend. Full rules: `rules/writing-rules.md`.

---

## 2. Canonical vocabulary

| Term | Rule |
|---|---|
| Pico | The product and brand in prose. Company and domain: PicoFinds, picofinds.com |
| Pico AI Shopping Assistant | The App Store listing name, always in full on the listing |
| Pico Assistant | The theme app embed's name in the Shopify theme editor |
| merchant / shopper / implementer | The store that pays / the person asking in the widget / the agency, developer, or freelancer who sets stores up |
| conversation | The billing unit: a chat thread with at least one AI reply, counted once per shopper and device per 24 hours |
| synced catalog | Where every product card comes from. Stock is as of the last catalog sync |
| zero result phrases, weak click phrases | Requests to the assistant that returned no products, or products nobody clicked. Never "searches" alone, since Shopify reports search-bar terms |

Full table, banned near-synonyms, and distinctions: `rules/glossary.md`.

---

## 3. Status ledger

Legend: SHIPPED live now. PARTIAL partly live. IN BUILD decided and unshipped, mark "coming soon" or omit. ROADMAP vision, never a launch claim. OUT out of scope by decision, never claimed.

- Shopper widget: natural language requests, product cards, add to cart, one clarifying question, reply chips, comparison inside a reply, replies in the shopper's language with Arabic right to left, welcome, session memory on one device: SHIPPED.
- Dashboard: Overview, Analytics, Catalog, Integrations, Assistant voice controls, Plan & Usage, Settings, four roles: SHIPPED.
- Setup: Shopify OAuth, theme app embed, four-step checklist, sandbox store, setup skill for coding agents, Free plan, 14 day Growth trial with no card: SHIPPED.
- Shopify App Store listing and Shopify Billing: IN BUILD (submit week 1, live target week 3).
- Quota alerts at 80% and 100%, 10% grace, launcher pause, published conversation definition: IN BUILD.
- Yearly prices, the Scale tier, founding cohort discount: IN BUILD.
- Inventory webhook (week 1), sync failure email (week 2), first insight and weekly summary emails (week 4), proof capture point (week 6), monthly usage summary (week 8), words against the catalog check (week 10): IN BUILD.
- Paid usability sessions, interviews, case studies, partner page, partner share, deal registration, payouts: IN BUILD.
- Revenue attribution, GA4 export, holdout lift measurement, multi-store agency workspace, partner portal: ROADMAP.
- Human handoff, order and policy answers, WhatsApp and Instagram, white label, bounties, headless claims: OUT.

Line by line with weeks and triggers: `rules/feature-status.md`.

---

## 4. Claim hygiene ledger

Every superlative and capability claim passes `rules/do-not-say.md`. The five scoping drills that matter most:

- "Never makes things up" becomes "Product cards show names, prices, and stock from your synced catalog." The AI writes reply text, so prose can still describe a product imperfectly.
- "The only assistant that sticks to your catalog" becomes "Built around your synced catalog." Catalog grounding is table stakes.
- "Semantic search" or "understands what shoppers mean" becomes "An AI model reads the request, then Pico matches it to your catalog by keywords, synonyms, and price range." There is no vector search.
- "Shows what customers want that you don't sell" becomes "Shows phrases shoppers asked the assistant that returned no products or few clicks." A zero result can be a missing product or a product described in other words.
- "Live stock" becomes "Stock as of your last catalog sync."

---

## 5. What Pico is

Pico is an AI shopping assistant for Shopify stores. Shoppers describe what they want in plain language, and Pico replies with product cards drawn from the store's own synced catalog: image, name, price, stock label, and a View link, with one-tap add to the store's own cart. When a request is vague, it asks one clarifying question.

The merchant manages it from a seven-page dashboard. The Analytics page shows the discovery funnel from request to result, click, and cart, the top phrases shoppers used, and the zero result and weak click phrases. The Overview compares 30 days against the prior 30, with sync health.

It installs from the App Store through a theme app embed with no theme code to edit, and a four-step checklist confirms the widget was seen. A sandbox store with a sample outdoor gear catalog runs on the real API, so anyone can try it first. A downloadable setup skill lets Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity run the setup.

Plans are priced by conversations a month: Free 50, Growth 600 for $49, Pro 2,000 for $99, and Scale 6,000 for $299 (IN BUILD). Yearly plans give two months free (IN BUILD). Every feature is on every plan. Each plan connects one store.

The company is PicoFinds, an Egypt-based team selling in USD worldwide, USA first. Planning basis: founder-led, two people.

---

## 6. Feature matrix: what leads, what is table stakes

Scored on demand (wanted by one, some, most, all) against competitiveness (commodity, most vendors, a few others, unique), each on a -20 to +20 axis.

**Merchants.** The only Hero is cost the merchant can predict: the quota meter with a published conversation definition and no overage. Differentiators sit where US demand is low today: the sandbox store, the coding agent setup skill, discovery analytics on what shoppers asked the assistant, the right to left widget, the custom catalog API. Table stakes: natural language requests, product cards, add to cart, voice controls, the Shopify install, the free plan. Table stakes Pico lacks, in roadmap weight order: revenue attribution, human handoff, order and policy answers, GA4 and Klaviyo, proactive prompts. The one candidate that could differentiate is holdout lift measurement.

**Implementers.** The partner floor (recurring share, development store installs, directory listing, tier badges) is table stakes Pico does not yet have. Hero rows, none built: a multi-store workspace, case studies credited to the implementer, pay for managing client stores. Real differentiators today: the sandbox, the setup skill, and the paid usability engagement, which no vendor found offers.

**Demand drivers.** Merchants: the Shopper Words Test, a free first session where the merchant types 10 to 20 requests the way shoppers ask and reads the phrases that found nothing. Implementers: the Paid Usability Session, $150 for up to 90 minutes on a store they work on.

Detail: `reference/feature-matrix.md`.

---

## 7. Competitive market analysis

**Merchant slate:** Chatty, Shopify Inbox with the Inbox agent, Shopify Search & Discovery, Tidio with Lyro, build or hire, and Shopify's agentic commerce stack, plus a 22-name watchlist. The free native agent is the default comparison, on about 358,000 stores (StoreLeads, 2026). Reviewers praise responsive support and easy setup most, and complain most about billing surprises (16+), then setup and theme conflicts, slow support, made-up answers, and results never seen.

| Vector, 0 to 10 | Leader | Pico now | Pico target |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Easy setup with responsive help | Chatty 8.9 | 6.8 | 7.9 |
| 2. Support automation breadth | Tidio 8.9 | 1.3 | 1.3, by design |
| 3. Insight into what shoppers ask | Pico 8.3 | 8.3 | 9.1 |
| 4. Answers traceable to the catalog | Pico 7.7, Search & Discovery 7.1 | 7.7 | 8.4 |

**Implementer slate:** the Gorgias agency program, Shopify Inbox, Rebuy plus Search & Discovery, Klaviyo Customer Agent with K:Partners, a custom build with Shopify's AI Toolkit, and the Shopify Partner Program. No AI shopping assistant appears on 26 sampled agency stack pages. Every program found pays after a referral or a closed deal, mostly about 20% for 12 to 36 months.

| Vector, 0 to 10 | Leader | Pico now | Pico target |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Established partner economics | Shopify Partner Program 9.1 | 0.4 | 4.6 |
| 2. Presence in the stack agencies sell | Klaviyo 9.3 | 0.2 | 2.1 |
| 3. Paid from the first engagement | Build 6.9 | 0.0 | 8.8 |
| 4. Proof the implementer co-owns | Build 6.8 | 1.1 | 8.3 |

Scores are analyst judgments from cited evidence. Pico's merchant scores rest on documented capability, and its implementer scores on the current state, since nothing runs yet. Detail: `reference/competitive-analysis-merchants.md`, `reference/competitive-analysis-implementers.md`, `reference/competitor-battlecards.md`.

---

## 8. Ideal customer profile and buying committee

**Merchants, Level 1:** US Shopify stores whose shoppers need help choosing between many similar or technical products (health, sports and outdoor, pets, auto parts, consumer electronics), on Shopify's own search with no AI assistant. 100 or more products, 10,000 to 100,000 monthly sessions, a team of 1 to 10, about $150,000 to $3 million a year (planning bands). The owner is user, manager, and decision maker in one person. About 54,300 US stores after the catalog cutoff (calculated, one tracker).

**Merchants, Level 2:** growing brands already paying for a search, quiz, or chat app whose shoppers still miss products. 250 or more products, 100,000 to 1 million sessions, 10 to 50 people plus an agency. The committee holds: ecommerce manager (user), head of ecommerce (manager), founder (decision maker), and a fourth column, the implementer, who rarely signs and can block by never enabling the theme embed.

**Implementers, Level 1:** freelancers and small studios, 1 to 5 people, under $250,000 a year, 2 to 10 active client stores, often on Upwork and Fiverr, who sell app installs for about $100 and have no AI shopping assistant in their build. The freelancer decides alone, and the merchant client pays.

**Implementers, Level 2:** build and CRO agencies, 6 to 50 people, 10 to 100 active client stores, that have deployed AI chat before and want something repeatable. Developer (user), project or account lead (manager), agency owner (decision maker), merchant client (budget holder).

**Design partners.** Merchants: the founding cohort of 20 US stores. Implementers: the paid usability cohort of 30 sessions in 60 days.

Detail: `reference/icp-personas-merchants.md`, `reference/icp-personas-implementers.md`, `reference/market-sizing.md`.

---

## 9. Strategic verdicts (decided)

1. **Two standalone go-to-markets.** Merchants and implementers each have their own positioning, channels, and targets. Shopware 6 and custom stores wait for a deferred third run.
2. **USA first, global English next. The GCC is for later,** and opens only when the US founding cohort is full and at least 5 GCC stores ask for Pico in one quarter.
3. **Merchants: position on insight and traceability, not support automation.** Pico leads on what shoppers ask and on answers traceable to the synced catalog. It deliberately does not do handoff, orders, or policies.
4. **Implementers: position on paid-first and co-owned proof, not partner economics.** Pay for the first session, credit the case study, then offer the partnership.
5. **Open proof, never invented proof.** Every proof field invites the reader to check something now. Customer proof enters only with exact wording, a source, and recorded permission.
6. **No overage, ever.** Alerts, grace, pause. Billing surprise is the category's most frequent complaint.
7. **One value metric.** Plans differ only in conversations a month. No feature gating.
8. **No separate agency price.** Shopify Billing charges each store, so partners earn a share instead.

Full log with dates and reopen triggers: `ops/decisions.md`.

---

## 10. Value proposition: merchants

**Brand promise.** Shoppers find products from your catalog by asking in their own words, and you see what they asked for.

**Positioning.** Built around your synced catalog, with insight into what shoppers ask: the phrases shoppers used, how requests move from results to clicks and add to cart, and which phrases returned nothing or drew few clicks. Stated as what Pico is built around, never as something only Pico does.

| Pillar | Reasons to believe |
|---|---|
| 1. Shoppers ask in their own words | Matched to your catalog by keywords, synonyms, and price range. Cards you can check against the last sync. One clarifying question, one tap to cart |
| 2. See what your shoppers asked for | Discovery funnel. Requests that found nothing. Overview, 30 days against the prior 30 |
| 3. A low-risk start | Sandbox store before install. Free plan and a 14 day Growth trial with no card. Four-step setup, no theme code |

Nine drills with headlines and copy: `reference/value-proposition-merchants.md`.

---

## 11. Value proposition: implementers

**Brand promise.** We pay you to try Pico on a store you work on, and we credit your work when your client agrees.

**Positioning.** An AI shopping assistant built for the people who set up stores: a sandbox and a setup skill that cut setup hours, an Analytics page the client can see, a paid first session, and case studies credited to the implementer.

| Pillar | Reasons to believe |
|---|---|
| 1. Set up without touching theme code | Theme app embed, removed on uninstall. Setup skill for coding agents. Sandbox store |
| 2. Show your client what shoppers ask | Zero result and weak click phrases. Four roles. Overview with sync health |
| 3. Get paid to shape it | $150 a session. A case study that credits your work. 25% of each referred store's subscription for 24 months, 30% for lead partners |

Nine drills: `reference/value-proposition-implementers.md`.

---

## 12. Positioning statements

**Merchant core claim.** Pico shows merchants what their shoppers ask for, and answers shoppers with products drawn from the store's own synced catalog.

- Against AI sales and support agents: not another AI chatbot that tries to answer everything, a shopping assistant built around your synced catalog that shows you what shoppers asked for.
- Against search, quiz, and custom builds: not a smarter search bar, a conversation for shoppers who don't know a product's name.
- Against doing nothing: not one more app to manage, a low-risk way to see what your shoppers are asking for.

**Implementer core claim.** Pico pays implementers for a first session on a store they work on, and, with the client's permission, credits their work in the case study that follows.

- Against vendors with agency programs: not another affiliate program that pays after the referral, a paid session that starts before any referral exists.
- Against custom builds and the native agent: not a build you have to maintain, an app you set up in four steps or hand to your coding agent.
- Against offering nothing: not a new service line to build from scratch, a paid first session on a store you already work on.

**Defensibility.** Both leads are narrow and copyable. The merchant lead compounds only if Pico ships the loop that turns each zero result phrase into a catalog fix and shows whether the fix worked. The implementer lead compounds through credited case studies and repeat deployments across client stores.

**The two objections that matter most.** "Why not the free Shopify Inbox agent?" Pico costs more, and the case rests on what the merchant learns from what shoppers asked, checkable on the free plan. "Is the partner program real?" The terms are decided and published on picofinds.com/partners from week 6, and no partner has been paid yet, so the first payout on the 15th must land on time.

Detail: `reference/positioning.md`, `reference/positioning-verdict.md`, `reference/objection-handling.md`.

---

## 13. Customer journey funnels

Seven stages per audience. Merchants: stage 2 happens on the App Store and in AI answer engines, stage 4 holds an activation sub-funnel, stage 7 is a monthly charge that ends with an uninstall. Implementers: stage 4 is the paid usability engagement, stage 7 is the next client store.

| Stage | Merchant target, first 90 days | Implementer target, first 90 days |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Problem awareness | 25% of scorecard completions open the sandbox | Cold email reply rate 5%, LinkedIn acceptance 30% |
| 2. Solution discovery | Listing visit to install 3% | 10 qualified applicants per Upwork post |
| 3. Vendor evaluation | Sandbox visit to install 10% | Offers accepted |
| 4. Trial or engagement | Widget seen within 24 hours on 65% of installs, median under 20 minutes, trial to paid 15% by day 30 | 30 sessions by day 60, median setup under 30 minutes |
| 5. Value realization | 3 catalog fixes per founding store in 60 days | 15 interviews |
| 6. Expansion and advocacy | 10 unincentivized reviews by day 90, 20 founding stores by day 60 | 3 case study permissions from both sides, 15 partner sign-ups |
| 7. Renewal or repeat | Monthly uninstall rate under 15% | 10 implementers on a second client store, every payout on the 15th |

**Critical success factor, merchants:** the theme embed is switched on, on the live theme, and stays on. Shopify app embeds are off by default after install. **Primary blocker, implementers:** platform rules, Upwork's 24-month non-circumvention term and Fiverr's off-platform ban.

Detail: `reference/customer-journey-merchants.md`, `reference/customer-journey-implementers.md`, `innovation/metrics.json`.

---

## 14. Campaign and channel plan

**Merchant channels:** the Shopify App Store, content and search (including AI answer engines), and the product-led lifecycle. The Shopper Words Test is the top-of-funnel asset in each: listing screenshots, a worksheet guide, a guided sandbox tour. Channel engine: `reference/app-store-engine.md`.

**Implementer channels:** cold email (US recipients only in the first 90 days), LinkedIn messages sent by hand, and job posts on Upwork and Fiverr. The Paid Usability Session is the opener in each. Channel engine: `reference/outreach-engine.md`.

**Excluded, refuse and redirect:** paid ads, cold outbound to store owners, GCC or Arabic-market assets, LinkedIn automation or LinkedIn Ads, any partner pitch inside Upwork or Fiverr, cold email to UK sole traders or anyone in the EU, and Gulf agency outreach.

**Lead magnets:** the Shopify Store Findability Scorecard (merchants) and the Agency AI Shopping Readiness Scorecard (implementers), both on ScoreApp. Detail: `reference/marketing-campaigns.md`, `reference/lead-magnets.md`, `reference/launch-plan.md`.

---

## 15. Quick-reference cheatsheet

- **Merchant one-liner:** Pico shows merchants what their shoppers ask for, and answers with products from the store's own synced catalog.
- **Implementer one-liner:** Paid to test it. Credited when it works.
- **Merchant hook:** the Shopper Words Test. **Implementer hook:** the Paid Usability Session, $150 for up to 90 minutes.
- **Flagship differentiator, merchants:** zero result and weak click phrases from what shoppers asked the assistant.
- **Table stake to win:** setup in four steps through the theme app embed.
- **Proof points on file:** none. Use open proof: the sandbox, the plan page, Shopify's documentation, the setup skill file.
- **Plans:** Free 50, Growth $49 for 600, Pro $99 for 2,000, Scale $299 for 6,000 (IN BUILD). Yearly: $490, $990, $2,990 (IN BUILD).
- **Partner terms (IN BUILD, week 6):** 25% for 24 months, 30% at five active paying stores, 10% managed share, payouts on the 15th, $50 minimum.
- **Founding cohort:** 20 US stores, 50% off for 6 billing periods, opens 2026-12-01.
- **Default rival, merchants:** the free Shopify Inbox agent. Never disparaged.
- **Do not say:** increases sales, never makes things up, semantic search, live stock, checkout in chat, only, free forever, Pico Partner Program before week 6.
- **Always:** no em dashes, open proof labelled as checkable, stock as of the last catalog sync.

---

*End of the Pico GTM master context. When status changes, update the ledger in `rules/` first, then this file, then `ops/decisions.md`, then the copy.*


===== rules/glossary.md =====

# Glossary, canonical vocabulary

Used in the product, the dashboard, the docs, and every asset. Mirror it exactly.
last_reviewed: 2026-11-04

## Names

| Term | Rule |
|---|---|
| Pico | The product and brand in prose. Capital P, no "PICO", no "Pico AI" as a bare name |
| PicoFinds | The company and project name. Domain: picofinds.com. Contact: us@picofinds.com |
| Pico AI Shopping Assistant | The Shopify App Store listing name, in full on the listing and in App Store copy. It separates Pico from "Piko ‑ Pickup Reminder" |
| Pico Assistant | The theme app embed's name, exactly as it appears in the Shopify theme editor |
| AI shopping assistant | The category. Lowercase in prose |

## People

| Term | Rule |
|---|---|
| merchant | The store that installs and pays. Not "user" in copy, not "client" unless an implementer is speaking |
| shopper | The person asking in the widget. Never "customer" when the merchant could misread it as their own buyer list |
| implementer | Agencies of every kind, Shopify developers, theme developers, and freelancers. "Agency" alone excludes freelancers |
| partner, lead partner | An implementer accepted into the program, and one with 5 active paying stores. Only after the partner page is live in week 6 |
| founding cohort | The first 20 US merchant stores. Never "beta" or "early access program" |

## Product

| Term | Rule |
|---|---|
| conversation | The billing unit: a chat thread with at least one AI reply. Messages from the same shopper on the same device within 24 hours count once. Fair use: 50 AI replies |
| synced catalog | The source of every product card. Always "synced", because stock is as of the last catalog sync |
| product card | Image, name, price, stock label, and a View link |
| Analytics page, Overview, Catalog, Integrations, Assistant, Plan & Usage, Settings | The seven dashboard pages, capitalized as named |
| discovery funnel | Request to result, click, and add to cart, with step conversion |
| zero result phrases, weak click phrases | Requests to the assistant that returned no products, or products that drew few clicks |
| sandbox store | The sample outdoor gear catalog on the real API. Never "demo store" in copy |
| setup skill | The downloadable file a coding agent follows. Never "AI installer" |
| theme app embed | How Pico reaches the storefront. Never "plugin" or "script injection" for Shopify |
| quota meter | The usage bar on Plan & Usage |

## Programs and magnets

| Term | Rule |
|---|---|
| Shopper Words Test | The merchant demand driver. Capitalized, never "audit" |
| Paid Usability Session | The implementer demand driver: $150, up to 90 minutes |
| Client Store Findability Audit | The service an implementer can sell from the session's findings |
| Shopify Store Findability Scorecard, Agency AI Shopping Readiness Scorecard | The two ScoreApp lead magnets, named in full |
| open proof | A claim the reader can check now, labelled as checkable. Never presented as a customer result |
| proof log | The closed list of permissioned customer proof. Empty on 2026-11-04 |
| managed share, deal registration | The 10% share on stores a partner manages but did not refer, and the 90-day claim on a client store's myshopify domain |

## Banned near-synonyms

| Do not use | Why, and what to use |
|---|---|
| chatbot | Pico positions against "another AI chatbot". Use AI shopping assistant |
| semantic search, AI search engine | There is no vector search. Describe the matching |
| live stock, real-time inventory | Stock is as of the last catalog sync |
| checkout in chat | Pico adds to the store's own cart. Checkout stays in the store |
| Pico Partner Program, certified partner | No program name before week 6, and no certification exists |

## Distinctions that must never blur

- **Conversation vs AI reply.** The quota counts conversations. Zipchat bills per AI reply. Mixing them misstates every price comparison.
- **Search-bar zero results vs zero result phrases.** Shopify's Search & Discovery already reports search-bar terms with no results. Pico's report covers requests made to the assistant. Every insight claim depends on this line.
- **Referred vs managed store.** 25% or 30% for referred stores, 10% for managed ones, one share per store.
- **Add to cart vs checkout.** Pico ends at the store's own cart.

The distinction that matters most: Pico reports what shoppers asked the assistant, not what they typed in the search bar.


===== rules/feature-status.md =====

# Feature status ledger

Governs what can be promised. Update this file the moment status changes, before any copy follows.
Legend: SHIPPED (live now, present tense). PARTIAL (say what works today). IN BUILD (decided, unshipped: "coming soon", or omit). ROADMAP (vision, never a launch claim). OUT (out of scope by decision, never claimed).
last_reviewed: 2026-11-04
Source: the Pico Core Features Overview (2026-11-02) and the decision log. Week 1 starts 2026-11-09.

## Shopper widget
- Natural language requests, matched by keywords, synonyms, and price range: SHIPPED.
- Product cards with image, name, price, stock label, View link: SHIPPED.
- Add to cart from the card, in-stock variant picked, out-of-stock blocked: SHIPPED.
- One clarifying question for vague requests, suggested reply chips: SHIPPED.
- Product comparison inside a reply: SHIPPED. A comparison screen: ROADMAP.
- Replies in the shopper's language, switcher, Arabic right to left, widget text in 10 languages: SHIPPED. Translation of catalog text: OUT.
- Personalized welcome, session memory across a reload on one device: SHIPPED. Cross-device memory or order-history personalization: OUT.
- Semantic or vector search: ROADMAP. Proactive prompts on product pages: ROADMAP.

## Merchant dashboard
- Overview, 30 days against the prior 30, with sync health: SHIPPED. Revenue attribution: ROADMAP.
- Analytics: discovery funnel, top phrases, zero result and weak click phrases, product impressions: SHIPPED.
- Catalog sync on demand, retry, sync log, counts: SHIPPED.
- Assistant voice controls, tone guidelines up to 1,000 characters, preview: SHIPPED.
- Plan & Usage: quota meter, upgrade, cancel with a reason, 50% retention offer for two periods: SHIPPED.
- Quota alerts at 80% and 100%, 10% grace on paid plans, launcher pause, no overage: IN BUILD.
- Published conversation definition on the plan page and listing: IN BUILD.
- Roles: owner, admin, analyst, support: SHIPPED. Multi-store agency workspace: ROADMAP, built when 10 partners each have 3 or more active paying stores.
- Every feature on every plan: SHIPPED, and kept that way.

## Setup and platform
- Shopify OAuth install, theme app embed, four-step checklist: SHIPPED.
- Shopify App Store listing and Shopify Billing: IN BUILD. Submit week 1, live target week 3, buffer to week 6.
- Theme coverage: claimed through the theme app embed only. Tests on Dawn and Horizon: IN BUILD. Headless (Hydrogen): OUT, not claimed.
- Speed: measured Lighthouse difference on Dawn, budget 10 points, published on the technical one-pager: IN BUILD (week 1). "No impact": OUT.
- Inventory webhook subscription: IN BUILD (week 1). Until it ships, copy says "Stock as of your last catalog sync".
- Sandbox store, setup skill for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity: SHIPPED.
- Shopware 6 and custom catalog API: SHIPPED in the product, OUT of both go-to-markets (deferred third run).
- EGP pricing by InstaPay: SHIPPED for non-Shopify stores, OUT of both go-to-markets.

## Plans and billing
- Free 50, Growth $49 for 600, Pro $99 for 2,000, 14 day Growth trial with no card: SHIPPED.
- Yearly at two months free: $490, $990, $2,990: IN BUILD.
- Scale, $299 for 6,000 with an onboarding call, and custom plans above it: IN BUILD.
- Founding cohort discount, 50% for 6 billing periods by Shopify Billing subscription discount: IN BUILD (opens 2026-12-01).
- Paid plans free for testing on partners' development stores: IN BUILD (switched on at launch).

## Lifecycle build list
- Sync failure email: IN BUILD (week 2). First insight email and weekly summary: IN BUILD (week 4).
- Proof capture point at value realization: IN BUILD (week 6). Monthly usage summary: IN BUILD (week 8).
- Words against the catalog check, a public page: IN BUILD (week 10).

## Scope decisions
- Human handoff or live chat: OUT. Reopen if 5 of 20 founding stores ask, or 2 uninstall reasons in a month.
- Order status, returns, and policy answers: OUT by design. Pico is a pre-purchase assistant.
- WhatsApp and Instagram: OUT until the GCC opens.
- GA4 event export: ROADMAP, built with revenue attribution after the founding cohort. Klaviyo: ROADMAP.
- Holdout or A/B lift measurement: ROADMAP, the candidate that could answer lift claims honestly.

## Implementer program
- Paid Usability Sessions ($150) and interviews ($75): IN BUILD, posts from week 1, sessions from week 2.
- Case study permission forms and terms clause: IN BUILD (week 2).
- Partner page, 25% and 30% shares, 10% managed share, deal registration, payouts on the 15th: IN BUILD (week 6, after counsel review in week 5).
- Directory listing on picofinds.com/partners: IN BUILD, after a partner's first active paying store.
- Partner portal, tier badges, co-marketing, certification: ROADMAP. White label, cash bounties, client discounts at launch: OUT.

## Demo rule
Nothing marked IN BUILD, ROADMAP, or OUT may be screen-recorded, narrated, or shown as if a merchant could use it today. Label it on screen and in the script, or leave it out.


===== rules/do-not-say.md =====

# Do not say

The claim hygiene spine. Check every claim here before it ships. Left column is forbidden or risky, right column is the safe replacement. Never a ban without a replacement.
last_reviewed: 2026-11-04

## Hard bans

| Do not say | Say instead |
|---|---|
| "Increases sales." "Boosts conversion." "Pays for itself." "Drives revenue." Any ROI or lift figure | "See what shoppers asked for, what they clicked, and what they added to cart." Revenue attribution is not measured, and the dashboard says so |
| "Pico never makes things up." "Zero hallucinations." "100% accurate." | "Product cards show names, prices, and stock from your synced catalog." |
| "Live stock." "Real-time inventory." "Checks live stock." | "Stock as of your last catalog sync." Add "updated by webhook on Shopify" only after the inventory webhook ships |
| "Only recommends what is in stock." | "Shows stock on every card, and keeps out-of-stock items out of the cart." |
| "AI-powered semantic search." "Understands what shoppers mean." | "An AI model reads the request, then Pico matches it to your catalog by keywords, synonyms, and price range." |
| "Shoppers can buy right in the chat." "Checkout in chat." | "One tap adds the product to your store's own cart." |
| "Compare products side by side." | "Pico can compare products inside its reply." |
| "Pico remembers your shoppers." | "The conversation survives a page reload on the same device." |
| "Shows you what customers want that you don't sell." | "Shows phrases shoppers asked the assistant that returned no products or few clicks, which points to gaps in the catalog or in how products are described." |
| "Sounds exactly like your brand." | "Set personality, warmth, answer length, emoji use, clarification style, and up to 1,000 characters of tone guidelines." |
| "Fully multilingual." "Speaks every language." | "Replies follow the shopper's language. Widget text is translated for 10 languages." |
| "Works with any store." | "Built for Shopify." Shopware 6 and custom stores belong to a later go-to-market |
| "Installs itself." "No developer needed." "Zero setup." | "Install from the App Store and follow a four-step checklist. Developers can hand the setup to a coding agent with Pico's setup skill." |
| "No impact on speed." | The measured Lighthouse difference on Dawn, as published on the technical one-pager, once measured |
| "Free forever." "Unlimited." | "Free covers 50 conversations a month." |
| "One plan for all your stores." "Built for agencies." | "Each plan connects one store." |
| Any install, store, merchant, review, rating, or conversation count for Pico | Nothing. Pico is pre-launch. Use open proof from `ops/copy-bank.md` |
| Any testimonial, named merchant, logo, or case study | Nothing until the proof log has an entry with exact wording, source, and recorded permission |
| "Your store is losing sales." "Shopify's search is broken." | "Shoppers who can't find a product by browsing can ask for it." |
| "Smarter than Shopify search." Any claim that a Shopify tool lacks something | Do not compare. Describe what Pico does |
| "Cheaper than Chatty." "Unlike other chatbots." Any named comparison | No comparison in copy that customers see without a sourced, dated, page-loaded finding, rechecked before each use |
| "Pay with InstaPay." EGP prices in Shopify copy | Nothing. Shopify installs bill in USD through Shopify Billing |
| "No surprise charges. Pico pauses before it bills you more." before the pause ships | "A quota meter shows usage on the Plan & Usage page." Use the pause line once the quota behavior is SHIPPED |

## Implementer bans

| Do not say | Say instead |
|---|---|
| "Earn recurring revenue." "Guaranteed leads." Any income or traffic number | "Partners earn 25% of each referred store's subscription for 24 months." Merchants who ask for setup help are offered listed partners |
| "Join the Pico Partner Program" before week 6. "Certified partner." "White label." | "Paid usability sessions: we pay you $150 to install Pico on a store you work on and tell us what works and what breaks." |
| "We'll feature your agency in a case study." | "With your client's written permission, we write up what changed on their store and credit your work." |
| Any rate other than 25%, 30%, and 10% managed | The published terms only, quoted exactly |
| A partner invitation, outside link, or email request inside Upwork or Fiverr | Nothing on the platform. Implementers find picofinds.com/partners on their own |

## In video, demos, and screenshots
- Nothing IN BUILD, ROADMAP, or OUT appears on screen as usable. The pause at quota, yearly prices, Scale, and the partner page are labeled "coming soon" until shipped.
- Sandbox data is labeled as sample data on screen. No real store data without recorded permission.
- No caveat gets dropped for pacing. If the stock line needs "as of the last sync", it gets said.

## Claims that need scoping
- **"The only assistant that sticks to your catalog."** Counter-example: Manifest AI, Wantly, Fast Simon, and dozens of App Store listings describe catalog-only answers, and Lyro skips out-of-stock items. Safe form: "Built around your synced catalog."
- **"Only Pico shows unanswered questions."** Counter-example: Shopify Search & Discovery reports search-bar terms with no results and no clicks, and Tidio lists questions Lyro could not answer. Safe form: insight into what shoppers asked the assistant.
- **"The Arabic AI shopping assistant."** Counter-example: Arabic-first Shopify apps exist (Luma, shamz.ai), Salla ships Arabic AI search, Fin and Lyro answer in Arabic. Safe form: "Arabic replies display right to left, with a language switcher and separate merchant copy per language." GCC copy only, later.
- **"No vendor pays implementers before a referral."** Holds for every program found on 2026-11-03, internally. In copy, describe Pico's offer, never the others'.
- **"A sandbox no competitor offers."** Holds for the slates checked on 2026-11-03. Internal only, and recheck before any use.

## Historical and reputational material
- picofinds.com led with Shopware, Arabic, and Egypt, and carried three lines broader than the product supports. The replacements above are the fix. Handle it, do not repeat the old lines.
- The listing name is "Pico AI Shopping Assistant" because "Piko ‑ Pickup Reminder" exists. Never shorten it on the listing.


===== rules/writing-rules.md =====

# Writing rules

These apply to every word of output, for both audiences, with no exceptions.
last_reviewed: 2026-11-04

## Mechanics
- No em dashes anywhere. Use commas, or restructure the sentence.
- Banned words: leverage, unlock, seamless, robust, streamline, cutting-edge, empower. No obvious variants either.
- Also avoid the slop list in `.claude/skills/gtm-slop-filter/SKILL.md`: elevate, revolutionize, game-changing, best-in-class, world-class, supercharge, harness, delve, utilize, myriad, plethora, pivotal.
- Short paragraphs, one to three sentences. Prose over lists, unless the content is a list.
- Specific numbers, named pages, and checkable facts over adjectives. "Free covers 50 conversations a month", never "generous free plan".
- No stacked adjectives, no hype, no superlative that `do-not-say.md` has not cleared.
- Prices with the unit: "$49 a month for 600 conversations". Percentages as numerals: 25%.

## Tone
Plain, exact, and a little dry. Merchants have been burned by app bills that grew without warning and by AI answers they could not check, so every sentence should be checkable in under a minute. Implementers carry the support burden of anything they recommend, so write like a peer offering paid work, not a vendor asking for a favor.

## Merchant copy
- Lead with the shopper's words and what the merchant gets to see. The insight is the product.
- Name the page: the Analytics page, the Overview, Plan & Usage. Named pages are checkable.
- Every merchant call to action points at the App Store listing once it is live. Until then, "Connect your store" on picofinds.com.

## Implementer copy
- Scope and fee in the first line: "$150 for up to 90 minutes."
- Quote the terms exactly: 25% for 24 months, 30% for lead partners, 10% managed share.
- Write the platform rule into the asset. On Upwork and Fiverr, no partner pitch, no outside link, no email request.

## Writing for the ear (demos, walkthrough videos, LinkedIn video)
- Short spoken sentences, contractions, second person. Talk to one listener.
- Front-load the point. Listeners cannot re-read.
- Read it aloud before it ships. If you stumble, cut it.
- Say the caveat out loud: "stock as of your last sync" survives pacing.

## Claim discipline
Every "only", "first", "best", "never", and "no other" goes through `do-not-say.md`. Every capability goes through `feature-status.md`: IN BUILD gets "coming soon" in the same sentence, or the sentence goes. A conditional claim names its condition: "on Shopify", "on paid plans", "from week 6".

## Open proof
Every proof slot carries open proof: something the reader can check now, and where. Label it as checkable, for example "Open the sandbox and try it." Never phrase open proof as a customer result.

## Channel discipline
This GTM writes for the Shopify App Store, content and search, the product-led lifecycle, cold email to US implementers, hand-sent LinkedIn messages, and Upwork and Fiverr job posts. It refuses paid ads, cold outbound to store owners, GCC or Arabic-market assets, LinkedIn automation, LinkedIn Ads, partner pitches inside Upwork or Fiverr, and cold email to UK sole traders or the EU. Refuse plainly and offer the in-scope channel.

## Signature lines (approved)
- "Pico finds it in your catalog."
- "See what your shoppers asked for."
- "Built around your synced catalog."
- "Paid to test it. Credited when it works."
- "Pico answers product questions. Keep your help desk for orders and people."
- "Stock as of your last catalog sync."

## Formatting
Headlines short and concrete, sentence case. One call to action per asset. No emoji unless the channel calls for it.


===== ops/QA-checklist.md =====

# QA checklist, run before shipping any output

Go through every item against the draft. Each one is answerable yes or no by looking at the draft. If any item fails, fix the draft, then run the list again. Machine pass first: `python3 tools/brain.py lint <file>`.

## Writing
- [ ] No em dashes anywhere.
- [ ] None of the banned words: leverage, unlock, seamless, robust, streamline, cutting-edge, empower, or a variant.
- [ ] Paragraphs of one to three sentences. Numbers and named pages instead of adjectives.
- [ ] Every price carries its unit, for example "$49 a month for 600 conversations".

## Channel
- [ ] The asset is for an in-scope channel: App Store, content and search, product-led lifecycle, cold email to US implementers, hand-sent LinkedIn, Upwork or Fiverr job posts.
- [ ] Not paid ads, not cold outbound to store owners, not GCC or Arabic-market, not LinkedIn automation, not cold email to UK sole traders or the EU. If it is, stop and redirect.
- [ ] On Upwork or Fiverr: no partner pitch, no outside link, no email request.
- [ ] Cold email: sender identity, an advertisement notice, the US postal address, and a working opt-out.

## Claims
- [ ] No revenue, sales, conversion, ROI, or lift claim about Pico or a client.
- [ ] No install, review, rating, or merchant count, and no testimonial or named merchant.
- [ ] Every capability mentioned is SHIPPED in `rules/feature-status.md`, or carries "coming soon" in the same sentence.
- [ ] The quota pause line appears only if the pause behavior is SHIPPED.
- [ ] Stock is "as of your last catalog sync", never live.
- [ ] Every "only", "first", "best", "never", and "no other" is cleared by `rules/do-not-say.md`.
- [ ] Every proof slot uses open proof that names what to check and where, and none reads as a customer result.
- [ ] No named competitor comparison, and nothing about what a Shopify tool lacks.
- [ ] Partner terms, if any, quoted exactly: 25% for 24 months, 30% for lead partners, 10% managed share.

## Naming and strategy
- [ ] Vocabulary matches `rules/glossary.md`: Pico, Pico AI Shopping Assistant, conversation, synced catalog, zero result phrases.
- [ ] Nothing contradicts a decided verdict in `ops/decisions.md`: USA first, GCC later, no overage, every feature on every plan, open proof.

## Audience and stage
- [ ] One audience only, merchants or implementers, never both.
- [ ] Copy matches the funnel stage in `reference/customer-journey-merchants.md` or `reference/customer-journey-implementers.md`.
- [ ] Exactly one call to action.

## Video and demos
- [ ] Read aloud without stumbling.
- [ ] Nothing IN BUILD, ROADMAP, or OUT shown as usable, and sandbox data labeled as sample data.

## Voice
- [ ] Reads like the matching file in `examples/`.

## After shipping
- [ ] Asset filed in `pages/` or listed in `ops/asset-index.md`.
- [ ] Anything the work taught you logged in `ops/signal-log.md`, and an `asset.shipped` event added with `python3 tools/brain.py event asset.shipped`.


===== ops/copy-bank.md =====

# Copy bank, approved language

Pre-approved lines, safe to reuse verbatim. Every line has passed `rules/do-not-say.md`. Lines tagged `[IN BUILD]` may ship only once the capability is SHIPPED in `rules/feature-status.md`. Rewriting an approved line turns a checked claim into an unchecked one.

When a decision changes a claim, grep this file for the old phrasing first.

## One-line positioning
- Merchants: "Pico shows merchants what their shoppers ask for, and answers shoppers with products drawn from the store's own synced catalog."
- Merchants, listing headline: "An AI shopping assistant for Shopify that answers from your own catalog."
- Merchants, short: "Pico finds it in your catalog."
- Implementers: "Pico pays implementers for a first session on a store they work on, and, with the client's permission, credits their work in the case study that follows."
- Implementers, short: "Paid to test it. Credited when it works."

## Reframes
- "Not another AI chatbot that tries to answer everything, a shopping assistant built around your synced catalog that shows you what shoppers asked for."
- "Not a smarter search bar, a conversation for shoppers who don't know a product's name."
- "Not one more app to manage, a low-risk way to see what your shoppers are asking for."
- "Not another affiliate program that pays after the referral, a paid session that starts before any referral exists."
- "Not a build you have to maintain, an app you set up in four steps or hand to your coding agent."
- "Pico answers product questions. Keep your help desk for orders and people."

## Hooks
- "Let shoppers describe what they need."
- "See the requests that found nothing."
- "Try it before you install anything."
- "We pay you $150 to install Pico on a store you work on and tell us what works and what breaks."
- "Show clients what their shoppers couldn't find."

## Merchant headlines
- "For shoppers who don't know the product's name."
- "Every card comes from your synced catalog."
- "From question to cart in one tap."
- "See where requests stop between question and cart."
- "Find out what shoppers looked for and missed."
- "Your last 30 days against the 30 before."
- "Start free with 50 conversations a month."
- "Four steps from install to live widget."
- "No theme code to edit."
- `[IN BUILD]` "No surprise charges. Pico pauses before it bills you more."

## Implementer headlines
- "Install without editing theme code."
- "Hand setup to your coding agent."
- "Test it before any client store."
- "Bring your client their shoppers' own words."
- "Give each person the access they need."
- "A month-on-month view for your client report."
- "Paid to test Pico on a store you work on."
- "A case study that credits your work."
- `[IN BUILD, week 6]` "25% of each referred store's subscription, for 24 months."

## Proof points (customer proof, the closed set)
None on 2026-11-04. The proof log is empty and closed. Anything that reads as a customer result is fabrication.

## Open proof (checkable now, use as-is)
- "Open the sandbox before you install anything." The Sandbox link in picofinds.com's top menu runs a sample outdoor gear catalog on Pico's real API.
- "Ask the sandbox in your own words, then check what it matched."
- "Open any card and check it against the catalog." Every sandbox card has a View link.
- "Give the sandbox a vague request and see what it asks."
- "Read the setup skill before your agent runs it."
- "Read Shopify's own docs on app embeds before you install."
- `[IN BUILD]` "The plan page states each plan's quota and what counts as one conversation."

## Calls to action
One per asset, never stacked.
- Merchants, before the listing is live: "Connect your store". After: "Install free from the Shopify App Store".
- Merchants, evaluation: "Open the sandbox store". Lead magnet: "Get my Findability Score".
- Implementers: "Apply for a paid session". "Download the setup skill". "Read the technical one-pager". `[IN BUILD, week 6]` "Read the terms on Pico's partner page".

## Customer language (verbatim, promoted from the signal log)
None yet. Real phrasing from merchants and implementers lands here only after it appears in `ops/signal-log.md` and passes triage.


===== ops/decisions.md =====

# Decision log

What was decided and why, so settled strategy is not relitigated. Newest at the top. Decision IDs (D1 to D56) are stable identifiers from the GTM build on 2026-11-03: cite them in commits, signals, and experiments. Every entry carries its reopen trigger, which `innovation/tripwires.json` encodes so the accounting layer can flag it automatically.

Types: **Decision** is a call Pico controls. **Researched** is a sourced fact. **Assumption** is a planning number nobody publishes, never used in customer copy, measured where it says.

---

## 2026-11 This repository is the go-to-market source of truth (DECIDED)
**IDs:** B1. Decided 2026-11-04.
The PicoGTMBrain repository holds the governed go-to-market for both audiences. Strategy, claims, status, and voice are changed here first, in the order ledger, master context, decision log, copy. `CLAUDE.md` wins if the routers disagree.
The GTM build produced dashboards, a walkthrough, and a Google folder. Those are deliverables. This repo is the operating system that keeps them true.
**What this does not change:** any decision below, any price, any target, any channel.
**Downstream:** the Google folder documents and the walkthrough are regenerated from this repo's ledgers when a ledger changes. Owner: founder.
**Reopen when:** never.

## 2026-11 Launch calendar and build list (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D56 and the launch calendar. Decided 2026-11-03.
Week 1 starts Monday 2026-11-09. Build order: inventory webhook (week 1), sync failure email (2), first insight email and weekly summary (4), partner ledger, payout run, and proof capture point (6), monthly usage summary (8), the words against the catalog check (10). The founding cohort opens 2026-12-01, after Cyber Monday. Day 60 review in week 12, day 90 review in week 13.
Each item is the touch-point for one funnel stage, sequenced so sync works before installs and partner tooling before the partner page.
**What this does not change:** prices, the partner terms, the channels.
**Reopen when:** an item slips by more than two weeks. The founder and engineer move the next block's scope.

## 2026-11 Planning bands where trackers are silent (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D53, D54, D55. Decided 2026-11-03.
Merchant Level 1: 100 or more products, 10,000 to 100,000 monthly sessions, 1 to 10 people, about $150,000 to $3 million a year. Level 2: 250 or more products, 100,000 to 1 million sessions, 10 to 50 people. 2% of sessions start a conversation (Assumption). Implementer Level 1: 1 to 5 people, under $250,000, 2 to 10 client stores. Level 2: 6 to 50 people, $1 million to $20 million, 10 to 100 client stores (Assumption).
Catalog cutoffs are researched (StoreLeads, 2026: 28.2% of stores sell 100 or more products). Sessions decide the band, because order values differ.
**What this does not change:** any customer copy. Bands never appear in copy.
**Reopen when:** the founding cohort's intake answers and first 30 days of conversations, and the first 30 session applications.

## 2026-11 Legal and platform conduct (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D47 to D52. Decided 2026-11-03.
A US private mailbox in Pico's name is the postal address on every commercial email from week 1. Cold email goes to US recipients only in the first 90 days, then UK companies and LLPs only, never UK sole traders, never cold to the EU. Sessions found on a platform are paid on that platform, and no partner invitation goes inside Upwork or Fiverr. Counsel reviews the partner terms in week 5. Permission forms and a terms clause are ready in week 2. Invoice-paid implementers sign a session agreement and give a W-9 or W-8BEN.
CAN-SPAM needs a postal address and an opt-out. PECR treats sole traders as individuals. Fiverr bars steering off the platform, and Upwork's term covers payments for 24 months.
**What this does not change:** the fee, the shares, the channel mix.
**Reopen when:** counsel advises otherwise, or either platform changes its terms.

## 2026-11 Listing, reviews, targets, and feedback cadence (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D42 to D46. Decided 2026-11-03.
The listing is "Pico AI Shopping Assistant" in the Chat category, search terms AI shopping assistant, product finder, product discovery. Screenshots lead with the Shopper Words Test, then cards, then Analytics, then the plan page. Reviews are asked for only after the merchant has opened Analytics and made one fix, replies within 2 business days, no incentives. Merchant and implementer 90-day targets are in `innovation/metrics.json`. Founding merchants get a monthly 30-minute call, partners a quarterly call and a digest after each batch of 10 sessions.
Merchants compare chat apps first, and the first reviews set the listing's tone.
**What this does not change:** the conversation definition or any price.
**Reopen when:** listing visit to install falls below 2% at day 30, or call attendance falls below half.

## 2026-11 Partner program terms and operations (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D35, D36, and D38 to D41. Decided 2026-11-03.
25% of each referred store's subscription charges for 24 months, 30% for lead partners at 5 active paying stores, 10% managed share, one share per store, no cash bounty. Payouts monthly on the 15th for charges Shopify paid out the prior month, $50 minimum carried forward, PayPal or bank transfer. Attribution by deal registration on the myshopify domain, merchant-confirmed, valid 90 days. Referral traffic is routed setup requests, never a promised volume. No separate agency price. The partner page goes live in week 6.
Above the 20% floor that Gorgias and Shopify set. A recurring share pays only while the store pays.
**What this does not change:** merchant prices, and Shopify Billing charging each store.
**Reopen when:** 12 months in, partner-referred stores pass 25% of paying stores, 2 attribution disputes in a quarter, or 50 routed requests a month.

## 2026-11 Paid sessions, interviews, and the session cohort (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D33, D34, D37. Decided 2026-11-03.
$150 for a fixed scope of up to 90 minutes: sandbox, install on a development or permissioned client store, the Shopper Words Test, timed setup, feedback form. Pico pays platform fees. Optional $75 interview for 30 minutes. 30 sessions in 60 days from week 1: Upwork 15, Fiverr 5, email 6, LinkedIn 4.
About $100 an hour, inside the research incentive range for engineers and above the roughly $100 gig for installing an AI chat app.
**What this does not change:** the partner terms.
**Reopen when:** fewer than 10 qualified applicants per Upwork post (raise to $200), fewer than half accept the interview, or day 30 completion rates by channel.

## 2026-11 The 90-day budget and the runway gate (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D31, D32. Decided 2026-11-03.
$9,000 over 90 days, capped at $3,000 a month: sessions $4,984, interviews $1,215, ScoreApp and Sales Navigator $477, sending domain and US mailbox $180, counsel $1,000, held back $1,144. Spend is released in 30-day blocks, each needing 6 months of company runway after it. If a block fails, paid sessions pause and outreach continues on email, LinkedIn, and the scorecard.
**What this does not change:** company burn, which sits outside the plan.
**Reopen when:** each 30-day block, and the day 90 review.

## 2026-11 The founding cohort (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D30. Decided 2026-11-03.
20 US stores, 50% off any paid plan for 6 billing periods through a Shopify Billing subscription discount, a monthly feedback call, a direct line to the founder, roadmap input. A written case study request at day 60. Opens 2026-12-01 and closes at 20 stores or 90 days after the listing goes live.
**What this does not change:** list prices.
**Reopen when:** it fills before day 60: open a second cohort of 20.

## 2026-11 Pricing structure (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D26 to D29. Decided 2026-11-03.
Yearly plans give two months free: Growth $490, Pro $990, Scale $2,990. Scale is $299 a month for 6,000 conversations with an onboarding call, and custom plans above it at about $0.05 a conversation. Model cost ceiling $0.02 a conversation (Assumption), which puts gross margin before other costs at 76% on Growth and 60% on Pro and Scale. Month 6 target mix: Free 60% of active installs, paying stores 70% Growth, 22% Pro, 8% Scale.
**What this does not change:** Free, Growth, and Pro monthly prices.
**Reopen when:** fewer than 10% choose yearly by month 6, 3 stores request a custom plan, measured model cost exceeds the ceiling in the first 30 days of logs, or the month 6 mix review.

## 2026-11 What a conversation is, and what happens at the quota (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D24, D25. Decided 2026-11-03.
A conversation is a chat thread with at least one AI reply, counted once per shopper and device per 24 hours, fair use 50 AI replies. At the quota: alerts at 80% and 100%, open conversations finish, paid plans get 10% grace at no charge, then the launcher pauses until the next cycle or an upgrade. No overage charge, ever.
Billing surprise is the category's most frequent complaint class, so a capped quota becomes a positioning line once it ships.
**What this does not change:** the plan prices.
**Reopen when:** 3 support tickets about the definition in a month, or pauses drive more than 20% of uninstall reasons.

## 2026-11 One value metric, development stores, and the workspace trigger (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D21, D22, D23. Decided 2026-11-03.
Every feature is on every plan, and plans differ only in conversations a month. Paid plans are free for testing on partners' development stores. The multi-store workspace is built when 10 partners each have 3 or more active paying stores, and until then a partner takes the admin role on each store.
**What this does not change:** one store per plan.
**Reopen when:** a feature needs gating to protect margin, or the workspace trigger fires.

## 2026-11 Product claims: themes, headless, speed, stock, catalog text (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D16 to D20. Decided 2026-11-03.
Theme claims cover Online Store themes through the theme app embed, tested on Dawn and Horizon before launch. Headless is not claimed. Speed budget 10 Lighthouse points on Dawn, measured in week 1 and published, never "no impact". Stock copy is "Stock as of your last catalog sync" until the inventory webhook ships. No claim that Pico translates catalog text.
**What this does not change:** the install path or the checklist.
**Reopen when:** a theme issue appears in 2 sessions, a Hydrogen store passes a session, the speed test fails the budget, or the webhook ships.

## 2026-11 Launch scope: handoff, orders, channels, integrations (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D12 to D15. Decided 2026-11-03.
Human handoff is not built or claimed. Order, return, and policy answers are out of scope by design. WhatsApp and Instagram wait for the GCC. The first integration is a GA4 event export, built with revenue attribution after the founding cohort.
Positioning against chat apps rests on not trying to answer everything.
**What this does not change:** the shopper widget's shipped capabilities.
**Reopen when:** 5 of 20 founding stores ask for handoff or order answers, or 2 uninstall reasons cite them in a month, or the GCC opens, or the founding cohort closes.

## 2026-11 Geography: USA first, the GCC on a trigger (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D11, owner decision 3. Decided 2026-11-03.
Global, USA first. The GCC opens when the US founding cohort is full and at least 5 GCC stores have asked for Pico in one quarter. Until then GCC material is reference only.
**What this does not change:** Arabic right to left as a shipped feature line.
**Reopen when:** the trigger fires: size the GCC and review messaging channels.

## 2026-11 Two standalone go-to-markets, slates stand, Shopware deferred (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D9, D10, owner decisions 5 and 8. Decided 2026-11-03.
Merchants and implementers each get a standalone go-to-market. Both competitor slates stand as built. Shopware 6 and custom stores wait for a deferred third run, and EGP prices appear in no merchant or implementer asset.
**What this does not change:** Shopware 6 and the custom catalog API as shipped product.
**Reopen when:** a slate slot fails its page-loaded check, or the third run starts.

## 2026-11 Operating basis and pre-launch state (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D5 to D8. Decided 2026-11-03.
An Egypt-based team selling in USD worldwide (Researched). Founder-led, two people (Assumption). No channel tried with results, and no installs, stores, payers, or rating recorded (Researched).
**What this does not change:** anything customer-facing. The team basis sizes timeframes only.
**Reopen when:** the team grows, the listing goes live, or the first 30 days of results arrive.

## 2026-11 Open proof, never invented proof (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D4, owner decision 2. Decided 2026-11-03.
The customer proof log is empty and closed. Every proof slot carries open proof: an invitation to check a claim now, naming what and where. A case study enters only with exact wording, a source, and recorded permission from everyone it names.
**What this does not change:** the narrowed claims, which still govern every line.
**Reopen when:** the first case study has recorded permission: it replaces the open proof line in its drill.

## 2026-11 Website and listing (DECIDED)
**IDs:** D1, D2, D3. Decided 2026-11-03.
Website: picofinds.com. The listing is submitted in week 1 as "Pico AI Shopping Assistant", live target week 3, buffer to week 6. Until it is live, every merchant call to action is "Connect your store". The site is aligned with the US-first plan before the first implementer email: Shopify and English first, Shopware on its own page, three broad lines replaced, new headline "An AI shopping assistant for Shopify that answers from your own catalog."
**What this does not change:** implementer sessions, which run on development stores and need no approved listing.
**Reopen when:** the listing is approved: every call to action switches to the listing.

---

## Open, owned elsewhere
- **Approve the six examples in `examples/` as voice references.** Owner: founder. Until approved they are proposed gold standards, five built only from copy-bank lines and the sync failure email written as the brain's live test on 2026-11-05.
- **Tone anchors.** Two brands whose voice is right for Pico, two that are wrong. Owner: founder.
- **Which AI tools the team runs.** Doors ship for 19 tools with their own file, for agents that read `AGENTS.md` such as Zed, Jules, and Amp, for MCP and HTTP clients, and for chat windows, rendered from one source, so a stale door fails CI instead of drifting. Prune the ones nobody uses from `RULE_DOORS` and `COMMAND_TOOLS` in `tools/brain.py`. Owner: founder.
- **Company runway and burn.** Outside the plan, read by the runway gate (D32). Owner: founder as CFO.
- **Counsel's review** of the partner terms, the session brief, and the platform conduct rules, week 5 (D50).
- **Shopware 6 connection wording.** The source says "Admin API access keys, optional sales channel key" in one place and "Admin API and Store API" in another. A status question for the third run.
- **Corroboration thresholds and ledger owners,** set to defaults in `ops/review-cadence.md` on 2026-11-04. Confirm or change.


===== reference/app-store-engine.md =====

# Channel engine, merchants: App Store, content, and product-led

Load first for any merchant channel task: listing copy, screenshots, catalog guides, comparison pages, lifecycle email, in-product strings. Synthesized from the merchant journey, assets library, and listing decisions.

## Thesis
Merchants decide on the App Store, in AI answer engines, and inside the trial. Pico has no reviews, so every channel hands the merchant something to check before trusting a claim: the sandbox, their own shoppers' words, the Analytics page. Activation, not awareness, decides whether an install becomes a paying store.

## How the three channels feed each other
Content and search bring merchants who already suspect shoppers miss products, and send them to the sandbox. The listing converts them with screenshots of the Shopper Words Test, cards, Analytics, and the quota. The product-led lifecycle carries them from install to widget seen, first conversation, first fix, and paid plan. Every fix and review feeds the listing's credibility.

## Archetypes to rotate
- **Words gap.** A shopper phrase, the product title it missed, the fix. Built only from sandbox or permissioned data.
- **Category guide.** How shoppers in health, outdoor, pets, auto parts, or electronics describe products, and how to name products so they are found.
- **When Pico fits and when it doesn't.** Honest comparison pages that name what Pico does not do. Facts sourced and dated.
- **Setup proof.** Four steps, the theme app embed, the checklist, the speed number once measured.
- **Quota clarity.** What a conversation is, what happens at the quota. The pause line only once shipped.

## The listing, field by field
Name "Pico AI Shopping Assistant". Category Chat. Search terms: AI shopping assistant, product finder, product discovery. Screenshot order: Shopper Words Test, product cards, Analytics, plan page with the quota. Introduction leads with the brand promise. Benefits follow the three pillars. Pricing states each plan's quota and, once shipped, the conversation definition and the no-overage rule. Demo store field: the sandbox.

## Plan, write, edit
1. **Plan.** One audience level, one stage, one pillar, one CTA. Pick the archetype.
2. **Write.** Start from `ops/copy-bank.md` lines. Name pages. Use sandbox examples labeled as sample.
3. **Edit.** Cut every sentence that would still read correctly with a competitor's name in it. Check every capability against `rules/feature-status.md`, every superlative against `rules/do-not-say.md`.

## Hook patterns
- The shopper's words: "waterproof hiking boots under $150".
- The merchant's own report: "Open 'Searches with no results' in your Shopify admin."
- The checkable claim: "Open any card and check it against the catalog."

## Calls to action
Before the listing is live: "Connect your store". After: "Install free from the Shopify App Store". Evaluation: "Open the sandbox store". One per asset.

## What good looks like
Listing visit to install 3%. Sandbox visit to install 10%. Widget seen within 24 hours on 65% of installs. First conversation within 7 days on 50%. Trial to paid 15% by day 30. Reviews asked only after the merchant has opened Analytics and made one fix. Review a channel on a full measurement cycle, never a single week.

## Never in this channel
Review incentives, fake urgency, outcome numbers, named competitors on the listing, Arabic or GCC screenshots, and paid ads.


===== reference/competitive-analysis-implementers.md =====

# Competitive analysis, implementers

Load for what an implementer recommends, installs, or builds instead of Pico, and the program behind each. Distills the implementer Competitive Market Analysis (2026-11-03). Implementers are analyzed as segments and counts, never as a named prospect list. Program terms change on notice and several pages conflict.

## The slate

| Offer | Program terms | Strength | Weakness |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gorgias Shopping Assistant, agency program | 20% for 2 to 3 years, Partner, Premier, Elite tiers, 15% Elite bounty. Conflict: one agreement lists 10% to 15% | On 13 of 26 sampled agency stack pages. Partner manager, events, co-marketing | Client billing surprises fall on the agency. The share freezes without a closed deal a year |
| Shopify Inbox with the Inbox agent | No app partner program | Free, native, nothing to maintain. A one-sentence recommendation | No revenue for the implementer. Client complaints on accuracy and handoff |
| Rebuy plus Search & Discovery | Referral 5% to 15% for 12 months, plus 5% managed while the agency works with the brand | On 7 of 26 pages. About 15,200 installs, up 24.7%. Pays for managing | Recommendations come from behavior, not from what shoppers say |
| Klaviyo Customer Agent, K:Partners | Master-track tiers by referred, platform, and managed MRR. Share not published | On 17 of 26 pages, the most of any app. Client health dashboards | Requirements grow with each tier |
| Build with Shopify's AI Toolkit | Billable hours. Freelance builds $30 to $1,000, agency builds $8,000 to $90,000 (vendor-sourced) | Full control, billable work | Maintenance and migrations stay with the builder |
| Shopify Partner Program | 20% of a referred merchant's subscription, $2,500 per qualifying Plus referral, launch partners 20% plus 0.1% of GMV for 4 years since 2026-08-10 | Every implementer is already in it, and its directory is where merchants find agencies | Commission confusion in community threads |

Watchlist, 13 names: Rep AI, Zipchat, Tidio, Intercom, Octane, Fast Simon, Nosto, Recharge, Okendo, LoyaltyLion, Voiceflow, Chatbase, and freelance gigs as a segment.

## What implementers value and resent
- Value: a vendor tier the agency can display (11 of 26 sampled pages show tiers), integration with the client's core stack, leads from vendor directories, paid implementation work.
- Resent: commission confusion and payout problems, requirements that grow, the support burden when a recommended app misbehaves, app sprawl and theme residue after uninstall.

## Positioning vectors, 0 to 10

| Vector | Pico now | Gorgias | Inbox | Rebuy+S&D | Klaviyo | Build | Shopify PP |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Established partner economics | 0.4 | 8.7 | 0.3 | 7.4 | 8.3 | 1.8 | 9.1 |
| 2. Presence in the stack agencies sell | 0.2 | 8.1 | 5.2 | 6.6 | 9.3 | 3.4 | 9.6 |
| 3. Paid from the first engagement | 0.0 | 3.4 | 0.0 | 4.8 | 2.1 | 6.9 | 2.9 |
| 4. Proof the implementer co-owns | 1.1 | 6.3 | 0.6 | 4.1 | 5.9 | 6.8 | 6.4 |

Pico's column is its current state: nothing in the program runs yet. Targets for the planned design: 4.6, 2.1, 8.8, 8.3.

## Where each leader wins
- Partner economics (Shopify Partner Program): a known share and a tier make yes easy.
- Stack presence (Klaviyo): the app already in the client stack wins by default.
- Paid first (build today, Pico by design): paying for the first session turns a cold message into paid work, the reason to reply.
- Co-owned proof (build today, Pico by design): a credited case study is the implementer's marketing, so they stay.

## The only element no offer has
The paid usability engagement. Every program found pays after a referral or a closed deal. Planned, not running, so it is never described as established.

## Platform rules that shape the route
Upwork: a 24-month non-circumvention term on relationships found there. Fiverr: no off-platform payment or steering. LinkedIn: no automation. CAN-SPAM: sender identity, advertisement notice, postal address, opt-out within 10 business days. Detail: `outreach-engine.md`.


===== reference/competitive-analysis-merchants.md =====

# Competitive analysis, merchants

Load for market context, competitor questions, and claim scoping in merchant copy. Distills the merchant Competitive Market Analysis (2026-11-03). Facts were read through a web search index and carry the date checked. Recheck any fact on the vendor's own page before it appears in copy.

## The slate

| Offer | What it is | Strength | Weakness |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chatty | AI sales agent with live chat, helpdesk, cart recovery, channels. Free plan with 50 AI conversations, about 1,900 reviews | Responsive support, easy setup, multi-language | Trial billing on reinstall, a slow bug fix, "needs daily attention" |
| Shopify Inbox with the Inbox agent | Shopify's free chat app with an opt-in AI agent, on about 358,000 stores | Free, native, on-brand answers, Shop sign-in personalization | One review of inaccurate answers asking for source visibility, handoff and reporting gaps |
| Shopify Search & Discovery | Free filters, synonyms, boosts, recommendations, semantic search for eligible stores, search analytics | Free and native, zero-result and no-click reports | 2.6 stars, 21% one-star reviews |
| Tidio with Lyro | Live chat, helpdesk, and Lyro in 48 languages, on about 27,500 stores | Easy setup, Lyro handles most questions | Lyro limits and billing disputes, slow support |
| Build or hire | An LLM wired to Shopify's catalog, cart, and order MCP servers, or staffed chat | Full control | Model use about $0.02 a conversation plus upkeep at 15% to 20% of the build a year (planning), 168 staffed hours a week is 4.2 agents |
| Shopify agentic stack | Products discoverable and buyable in ChatGPT, Copilot, AI Mode, Gemini, and Meta | Default reach, no channel fees per Shopify | The conversation happens off the store |

Watchlist, 22 names: Rep AI, Zipchat, Dialog, Alhena, Wizybot, Manifest, Verifast, Moose, Luma, Gorgias, Fin, Klaviyo Customer Agent, Fast Simon, Boost, Searchanise, Doofinder, Smart Product Filter & Search, Rebuy, Octane, RevenueHunt, Tolstoy, Zoko.

## What reviewers say across the set
- Praise: hands-on vendor support, easy setup, AI that resolves most questions.
- Complaints, most frequent first: pricing or billing surprise (16+), setup or theme conflict (12+), support responsiveness (8+), made-up answers (7+), results not arriving (7+).
- Frequency counts are reviews seen in indexed snippets, a floor rather than a census.

## Positioning vectors, 0 to 10

| Vector | Pico | Chatty | Inbox | S&D | Tidio | Build | Agentic |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Easy setup with responsive help | 6.8 | 8.9 | 8.3 | 6.2 | 7.4 | 3.1 | 7.6 |
| 2. Support automation breadth | 1.3 | 8.6 | 7.8 | 0.6 | 8.9 | 6.2 | 2.3 |
| 3. Insight into what shoppers ask | 8.3 | 4.1 | 3.7 | 6.1 | 6.6 | 4.4 | 1.6 |
| 4. Answers traceable to the catalog | 7.7 | 6.3 | 6.4 | 7.1 | 5.8 | 4.9 | 6.2 |

Vectors 1 and 2 come from what reviewers praise, where competitors lead. Vectors 3 and 4 reverse the complaints Pico can address. Pico's scores rest on documented capability only.

## Where each leader wins acquisition
- Setup (Chatty): five-star reviews drive App Store ranking, and 1,900 reviews compound.
- Support breadth (Tidio): merchants buy one support tool and get shopping help with it.
- Insight (Pico, by capability): a merchant who sees the requests that found nothing has a reason to install before believing any sales claim. The Shopper Words Test turns this into the entry point.
- Traceability (Pico, narrowly): reviewers distrust answers they cannot check. Cards from the synced catalog plus a visible sync log give the merchant something to verify.

## Price per conversation, internal only
Pico Growth about $0.08, Pro and Scale about $0.05. Chatty about $0.14 to $0.20, overage $0.40. Lyro about $0.50 to $0.65, sources conflict. Verifast about $0.05 to $0.16 per chat. Zipchat about $0.11 per AI reply. Fin $0.99 per resolution. The Inbox agent is free. Features differ widely: never a copy line without a page-loaded recheck.

## Open questions
Many presence cells were "not found in the sources read". Confirm the slate columns with page loads before any comparative statement leaves this file.


===== reference/competitor-battlecards.md =====

# Competitor battlecards
