Load for sales calls, partner calls, review replies, and objection prep. Three lines per rival: their real strength first, their real gap, how Pico wins. Internal only. In copy that customers see, never name a rival and never say what a Shopify tool lacks.

## Merchants

**Shopify Inbox with the Inbox agent (the default comparison)**
- Strength: free, native, on about 358,000 stores, personalizes from Shop sign-in, and now starts checkout from chat.
- Gap: built for support breadth across orders and policies. Pico does not try to match it there.
- How Pico wins: the merchant sees what shoppers asked, the phrases that found nothing, checkable on the free plan. Pico costs more, and the case rests on what the merchant learns.

**Chatty**
- Strength: responsive support, easy setup, a 50-conversation free plan, about 1,900 reviews, selling plus helpdesk in one app.
- Gap: reviewers cite billing surprises, and AI conversations cost about $0.14 to $0.20 with $0.40 overage.
- How Pico wins: a quota the merchant can see and, once shipped, a pause instead of overage. Insight into requests instead of a support inbox.

**Shopify Search & Discovery**
- Strength: free, in every store, semantic search for eligible stores, search-bar zero-result reports.
- Gap: built for the search bar. Shoppers who don't know a product's name have nowhere to describe it.
- How Pico wins: a conversation beside search, never instead of it. Speak well of the native report and use it in the Shopper Words Test.

**Tidio with Lyro**
- Strength: established support suite, 48 languages, about 27,500 stores, Lyro resolves most questions.
- Gap: reviewers report Lyro limits and billing disputes, and slow email support.
- How Pico wins: pre-purchase only, priced per conversation at a lower unit, with hands-on onboarding for the founding cohort.

**Build or hire**
- Strength: full control, a person can answer anything.
- Gap: the merchant carries model cost, upkeep, migrations, and staffing.
- How Pico wins: an App Store install with a four-step checklist, nothing to build or maintain.

**Shopify agentic stack**
- Strength: reach inside AI assistants by default, no channel fees per Shopify.
- Gap: the conversation happens off the store.
- How Pico wins: Pico is the conversation on the store, with the insight that comes from it. Complementary, never framed as a fight.

## Implementers

**Gorgias agency program**
- Strength: tiers agencies display, a partner manager, co-marketing, lead sharing, 20% for 2 to 3 years.
- Gap: the share freezes without a closed deal a year, and client billing surprises land on the agency.
- How Pico wins: paid before any referral, published terms, 25% for 24 months with good standing at one active paying store a year.

**Shopify Inbox**
- Strength: free, native, a one-sentence recommendation with no upkeep.
- Gap: the implementer earns nothing from it.
- How Pico wins: a paid first session, then a share on each referred store, plus something concrete to show the client.

**Rebuy plus Search & Discovery**
- Strength: pays a 5% managed share whoever referred the brand, and sits in more sampled stacks than any other discovery app.
- Gap: recommendations from behavior, not from what shoppers say.
- How Pico wins: client-visible phrases shoppers asked, in their own words, as CRO research input, and a 10% managed share.

**Klaviyo Customer Agent**
- Strength: already in 17 of 26 sampled stacks, client health dashboards.
- Gap: requirements grow with each tier.
- How Pico wins: one threshold to lead partner, 5 active paying stores, and a paid session that needs no tier at all.

**Build with the AI Toolkit**
- Strength: billable, fully owned work, with Shopify's own tools.
- Gap: maintenance and migrations stay with the builder.
- How Pico wins: four steps or a coding agent, with no build to maintain after handover, and the setup hours are paid in the session.

**Shopify Partner Program**
- Strength: every implementer is in it, and its directory is where merchants find agencies.
- Gap: commission confusion reported in community threads.
- How Pico wins: payouts on the 15th with a $50 minimum and deal registration the partner can check. Separate from Shopify's own earnings, which are unaffected.


===== reference/customer-journey-implementers.md =====

# Customer journey, implementers

Load to match outreach to a stage, run the paid engagement, or plan partner lifecycle messages. Distills the implementer Customer Journey Funnel (2026-11-03). Targets live in `innovation/metrics.json`. Week 1 starts 2026-11-09.

| Stage | Mindset and trigger | Touch-points | KPIs and targets (first 90 days) | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Problem awareness | "Clients keep asking me about AI chatbots, and I don't have a tested answer." | First email offering a paid session, LinkedIn message by hand, Upwork and Fiverr posts, Agency AI Shopping Readiness Scorecard | Cold email reply rate 5%. LinkedIn acceptance 30%, replies from 15% of accepted | Marketing |
| 2. Solution discovery | "Is this paid work real, and is the app any good?" The offer | Job post with fixed scope, partner page with session scope, sandbox link, setup walkthrough video | 10 qualified applicants per Upwork post, or the fee rises to $200 | Marketing and sales |
| 3. Vendor evaluation | "Can I install it without breaking anything, and is the fee worth my time?" | Technical one-pager, setup skill download, sandbox, client permission template | Offers accepted. Time from first contact to acceptance | Sales |
| 4. The paid engagement | "I'll install it on a store I work on and report back." The booked session | Session brief and feedback form, findings template, payment by Upwork, Fiverr, or invoice | 15 Upwork hires from 3 posts. 5 Fiverr orders. 30 sessions by day 60. Median setup under 30 minutes | Sales and CS |
| 5. Value realization | "My client saw the phrases their shoppers asked." The findings list | Interview, 30 minutes for $75. Client-facing one-pager. The Analytics page | 15 interviews. Client stores that keep Pico after the session | CS |
| 6. Expansion and advocacy | "I'd put this on another client store, and I want the case study." | Permission forms for merchant and implementer, the partnership offer on Pico's own pages, email, or LinkedIn | 3 case study permissions from both sides by day 90. 15 partner sign-ups by day 90 | CS and marketing |
| 7. Repeat deployment | "Next client store." A new client, a redesign | Partner ledger and payouts from week 6, portal at 25 partners, workspace on its trigger, monthly partner update | 10 implementers on a second client store by day 90. 100% of payouts on the 15th | CS and product |

## Stage 4, the engagement step by step

| Step | What happens | Platform rule or blocker | Intervention |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Recruit | Upwork fixed-price post, Fiverr brief or gig order, cold email, LinkedIn message | CAN-SPAM for email, no automation on LinkedIn | Scope and fee in the first line, messages by hand |
| 2. Accept | The implementer accepts scope and the $150 fee | Upwork keeps payments on Upwork for 24 months, Fiverr pays only by order | Pay on the platform where found |
| 3. Sandbox test | Sandbox store and setup skill | None | Setup walkthrough video |
| 4. Client permission | If a client store is used, the merchant agrees in writing | The client is the budget holder | One-page permission template, a development store as fallback |
| 5. Install | Checklist or setup skill | App embeds are off by default after install | Checklist prompts, a setup-time log |
| 6. Shopper Words Test | Phrases from the client's customers, read in Analytics | None | The findings template |
| 7. Feedback | What worked, what broke, setup time | None | Required fields in the form |
| 8. Payment | Within 7 days of the completed form, or milestone or order release | As step 2 | Pay on time, every time |
| 9. Interview | Optional, $75 | Same platform rule | Offer inside the same engagement |
| 10. Case study permission | Optional, from merchant and implementer | The proof rules | Exact wording to be published, in the form |
| 11. Partnership invite | From week 6: 25% for 24 months, 30% for lead partners | No invitation inside Fiverr. Upwork payouts stay on Upwork for 24 months | Open the program on Pico's own page, email, and LinkedIn. Counsel review in week 5 |

## Key insights
- **Critical success factors:** fee and scope in the first message. The install works first time on a real store. Client permission handled up front. Partnership terms ready before the first sessions end.
- **Blockers:** platform rules. A new program with no record, so the first payout on the 15th must land. Client permission. One store per plan until the workspace ships.
- **Accelerators:** start with freelancers who already sell installs for about $100. Shorten every session with the sandbox and setup skill. Turn the findings list into the Client Store Findability Audit. Switch on free development store testing before outreach starts.


===== reference/customer-journey-merchants.md =====

# Customer journey, merchants

Load to match copy to a funnel stage, plan lifecycle emails, or diagnose activation. Distills the merchant Customer Journey Funnel (2026-11-03). Targets live in `innovation/metrics.json`. Quotes are illustrative personas, not real merchants.

| Stage | Mindset and trigger | Touch-points | KPIs and targets (90 days after the listing is live) | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Problem awareness | "Shoppers keep emailing to ask which one fits." Repeat questions, a new line, peak prep | Shopper Words Test, Findability Scorecard, catalog guides, answers in AI assistants | Scorecard completions that open the sandbox: 25% | Marketing |
| 2. Solution discovery | "Dozens of AI chat apps. Which help shoppers choose?" A Shopify announcement, a roundup | App Store listing, comparison pages with sourced and dated facts, sandbox link | Listing visit to install: 3% | Marketing |
| 3. Vendor evaluation | "Will it say something wrong, break my theme, surprise me with a bill?" | Sandbox, plan page with every quota, the "what Pico does not do" list, technical one-pager | Sandbox visit to install: 10% | Product |
| 4. Trial | "Let me see it on my own store before I pay." The install | Four-step checklist, trial emails, in-dashboard prompts, setup skill | Widget seen within 24 hours: 65%. Median install to widget seen: under 20 minutes. Trial to paid by day 30: 15% of installs | Product and CS |
| 5. Value realization | "Shoppers are using it. What are they asking?" First week of conversations | Analytics, Overview, first insight and weekly summary emails (week 4), proof capture point (week 6) | Catalog fixes from the report: 3 per founding store in 60 days | CS |
| 6. Expansion and advocacy | "We hit the quota. Is Pro worth it?" The meter, a good month | Upgrade prompt, review request after a fix, case study invitation, referral to implementer partners | 10 unincentivized reviews by day 90. 20 founding stores by day 60 | CS and marketing |
| 7. Renewal | "Is this still worth it this month?" Each charge, a theme change | Monthly usage summary (week 8), embed check after theme changes, cancel flow with reason and retention offer | Monthly uninstall rate under 15%. Embed still active after a theme change: 90% | CS and product |

## Stage 4, the activation sub-funnel

| Step | What happens | Drop-off question | Target |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Install | Added from the App Store | Left at the permissions screen? | |
| 2. Authorize | OAuth, tokens stored encrypted | Did the installer have rights? | 95% of installs |
| 3. Enable the embed | Pico Assistant switched on in the theme editor. Embeds are off by default and live only on the theme where enabled | On, and on the live theme? | 70% within 24 hours |
| 4. Sync | Catalog sync with counts and log | Did any job fail? | 90% within 24 hours |
| 5. Widget seen | The checklist confirms a visitor saw it | Has anyone seen it yet? | 65% within 24 hours, median under 20 minutes |
| 6. First conversation | A shopper asks something | Are shoppers opening it? | 50% within 7 days |
| 7. Plan and quota | Trial ends, Free or a paid plan through Shopify Billing | Will the quota run out mid-month? | 15% on a paid plan by day 30 |

Interventions: a setup email with the checklist, an in-dashboard prompt linking to the theme editor, retry from the Catalog page, the sync failure email (week 2), an upgrade prompt at 80% of quota. At 100%, open conversations finish, paid plans get 10% grace, then the launcher pauses (IN BUILD). Never an overage charge.

## Key insights
- **Critical success factors:** the embed on, on the live theme, after every theme change. The first value moment inside the trial: the merchant opens the zero result phrases and recognizes a fix. The quota and the conversation definition clear before the first charge. A listing that earns installs before any review exists.
- **Blockers:** the embed left off. Free's 50 conversations running out mid-month. Paying by card in USD through Shopify Billing. The free Inbox agent as the default comparison while Pico has no reviews.
- **Accelerators:** start from the merchant's own words, the Words Test and the Scorecard into the sandbox. Implementers install for client stores. A proof capture point at the first fall in a store's zero result rate. An embed check after every theme change.


===== reference/feature-matrix.md =====

# Feature matrix, both audiences

Load to decide what leads a message, what is table stakes, and what is roadmap. Distills the two Product Feature Matrices (2026-11-03). Status of every row lives in `rules/feature-status.md`.

## The model
Each row is scored on demand (wanted by one, some, most, all) and competitiveness (commodity, most vendors, a few others, unique), each mapped to a -20 to +20 axis. Quadrants: Q1 Hero (high demand, high advantage), Q2 Differentiator (low demand, high advantage), Q3 Commodity (low, low), Q4 Table Stakes (high demand, low advantage). Three pairings are not allowed and were checked on every row: some with most vendors, all with unique, one with commodity. A candidate in any quadrant is a roadmap finding, never a claim.

## Merchants: 22 stated rows, 12 candidates

| Quadrant | Rows |
|---|---|
| Q1 Hero | 14 Quota meter and plan controls (7.3, 4.6), Hero once the conversation definition and no-overage rule ship |
| Q2 Differentiator | 6 Comparison in reply, 7 Shopper language with Arabic RTL, 11 Discovery analytics, 12 Sync log, 17 Shopware 6, 18 Custom catalog API, 19 Sandbox store (-0.6, 15.8), 20 Setup skill (-13.1, 14.6), 22 Egypt local payment, C3 Multi-store plan, C4 Comparison screen, C9 Holdout lift measurement |
| Q3 Commodity | 4 Clarifying question, 5 Reply chips, 8 Personalized welcome, 9 Session memory, 15 Roles, C7 WhatsApp, C10 Partner program, C11 Dev store installs |
| Q4 Table Stakes | 1 Natural language requests, 2 Product cards, 3 Add to cart, 10 Overview metrics, 13 Voice controls, 16 Shopify install and checklist, 21 Free plan and trial |
| Q4, missing | C1 Revenue attribution (14.9, -4.3), C2 Semantic search, C5 Human handoff, C6 Order and policy answers, C8 GA4 and Klaviyo, C12 Proactive prompts |

**What it says.** Pico's differentiators sit where US merchant demand is low today. The weightiest roadmap rows are table stakes Pico lacks: C1, C5, C6, C8. The one candidate that could differentiate is C9, holdout measurement, the only honest answer to the category's lift claims. In the GCC, row 7 would move toward Hero.

## Implementers: 7 product rows, 3 candidates, 12 program elements

| Quadrant | Rows |
|---|---|
| Q1 Hero, none built | C3 Multi-store workspace (11.7, 5.3), P3 Case studies with client stores (8.9, 3.7), P11 Pay for managing (10.2, 6.9) |
| Q2 Differentiator | 18 Custom catalog API, 19 Sandbox store, 20 Setup skill, 7 Per-language copy with Arabic RTL, 11 Client-visible analytics, P1 Paid usability engagement (-0.6, 17.2), P2 Paid interviews, P5 Co-marketing, P9 White label, P10 Client discount, P12 Partner manager |
| Q3 Commodity | P7 Certification and training |
| Q4 Table Stakes | 16 Theme app embed install, 15 Roles, P4 Referral traffic |
| Q4, missing | C10 Recurring revenue share, C11 Dev store installs, P6 Directory listing, P8 Tier badges |

**What it says.** The partner floor is table stakes Pico does not have yet. The real differentiators save hours before a client sees anything: the sandbox, the setup skill, and the paid engagement, which pays before any referral. Build order for program elements: dev store installs and the paid sessions first, then case studies, the share, and the directory, then tiers, managed pay, and the workspace on its trigger.

## Demand drivers

**Merchants: the Shopper Words Test.** A free first session: install on Free (50 conversations), type 10 to 20 requests the way shoppers ask, for example Shopify's own "Searches with no results" terms rephrased as questions, and read the requests that returned no products or few clicks. It separates a missing product from a product described in words the shopper did not use. Variants: findability review (white glove), sandbox tour, words against the catalog check (week 10), the Findability Scorecard, the implementer-run audit.

**Implementers: the Paid Usability Session.** $150 for up to 90 minutes: install Pico on a store they work on, run the Shopper Words Test with phrases from the client's customers, report what worked, what broke, and how long setup took. Paid on the platform where they were found. Variants: Client Store Findability Audit, sandbox developer test, setup walkthrough video, Agency AI Shopping Readiness Scorecard, co-authored case study.


===== reference/gcc-later.md =====

# The GCC, a secondary go-to-market for later

Load only when someone asks about the Gulf, Arabic-market copy, or the GCC trigger. Nothing here is pursued now, and no GCC copy, channel, or budget exists in the primary plan. Distills the GCC sheets of both ICP dashboards and the Arabic markets research (2026-11-03).

## The trigger
The GCC opens when the US founding cohort is full and at least 5 GCC stores have asked for Pico in one quarter (D11). `innovation/tripwires.json` watches for it: log every GCC inbound as a `SEGMENT` signal with `region: GCC`. When it fires, size the GCC from the UAE first and review messaging channels (D14).

## Merchants there
- Live Shopify stores: UAE 26,986, Saudi Arabia 4,480, Kuwait 3,790, Qatar 2,265, Bahrain at least 367, Oman at least 471. At least about 38,400 across the six (StoreLeads, 2026). Many UAE stores run English storefronts. Stores with an Arabic storefront are not published by any tracker, so it is asked at intake.
- Platform context: Saudi Arabia is mostly WooCommerce (36.8%), Zid (16.4%), and Shopify (13.5%) of detected sites, and Salla leads by store count elsewhere. Pico reaches Salla and Zid only through the custom catalog API.
- How shoppers ask: social and messaging heavy. 79% of UAE shoppers use social media to research products (secondhand). Pico has no WhatsApp channel.
- Competition: Arabic-first Shopify apps (Luma, shamz.ai), Verifast naming Arabic, Fin and Lyro answering in Arabic, Salla's own Arabic AI search, Meta's business agent on WhatsApp.
- Billing: Shopify Billing in USD, with no local-currency estimate for AED, SAR, KWD, or QAR.
- ICP if opened: UAE Shopify stores with Arabic or bilingual storefronts in the same help-me-choose categories.

## Implementers there
Partner Directory profiles in Dubai list Arabic right to left development as a service. The five UAE agency pages in the stack sample list local payment and WhatsApp setup, not chat apps. A Gulf agency can join the partner program through Pico's public page at any time, but there is no outreach.

## The one copy line, for later
"Arabic replies display right to left, with a language switcher and separate merchant copy per language." Merchant statement 1 and implementer statement 2 gain it when the GCC opens, and merchant pillar 1 gains a reason to believe.

## Never, now or later
"The Arabic AI shopping assistant." "Built for the Middle East." "GCC-ready." "Understands every Arabic dialect." No dialect handling is stated, and Arabic-first assistants already exist.


===== reference/icp-personas-implementers.md =====

# ICP and personas, implementers

Load for implementer targeting, outreach lists, session applications, and partner copy. Distills the implementer ICP Dashboard and Buying Committee (2026-11-03). Bands are planning assumptions asked in the session application (D55). Implementers are segments and counts, never a named prospect list.

## The two levels

| | Level 1: no AI shopping assistant in their build | Level 2: has deployed AI chat, wants something repeatable |
|---|---|---|
| Segment | Freelance Shopify developers and small studios who install apps for client stores, including on Upwork and Fiverr | Build and CRO agencies at Select or Plus tier and above that have set up AI chat for several clients |
| Location | Serving US stores, based anywhere | US-serving first, then UK, Canada, Australia. US directory, March 2026: 33 Platinum, 45 Premier, 255 Plus, 342 Select (secondary) |
| Bands (planning) | 1 to 5 people, under $250,000 a year, 2 to 10 active client stores, Registered or unlisted | 6 to 50 people, $1 million to $20 million, 10 to 100 client stores |
| How they charge | Fixed gigs and hourly. AI chatbot gigs $30 to $1,000, app installs about $100 | Projects and retainers, CRO fees sometimes tied to results |
| Pain | Income gig by gig, no credential beside the apps they install, no paid time to learn an app, clients ask about AI and they have no tested answer | Every app they recommend becomes their support burden. Programs that pay only after referrals. Theme residue. No proof to show for AI chat |
| Triggers | A client asks for an AI chatbot, an offer of paid work, Shopify AI news | An unhappy chat client, a redesign, next quarter's service lines, Shopify Editions and DotDev |
| Engagement | The paid session as a job on Upwork or Fiverr, or by email and LinkedIn | The paid session by email and LinkedIn, then a case study, then the partnership |

## The committee

**Level 1 collapses into the freelancer, and the merchant client pays.** The freelancer decides whether to take the session and whether to recommend Pico. Blocks: a fee below their time, unclear scope, fear of breaking a client store, a platform rule that risks their account, no reviews of Pico. Drivers: paid work on first contact, a tested AI answer, credit in a case study, early access to the partnership. Assets: the job post with fixed scope and fee, the sandbox, the setup skill, the technical one-pager. The client approves any install on their store and must see the findings list, the setup time, and that Pico installs with no theme code to edit. Pico never contacts the client directly.

**Level 2 holds, with the merchant client as budget holder.**

| | Developer | Project or account lead | Agency owner | Merchant client |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Influence | Recommends or vetoes on technical grounds | Recommends to the client, owns the case study | Decides on programs and the standard stack | Approves the install, pays the plan and the agency |
| Stages | 3, 4, 7 | 2, 4, 5, 6 | 1, 3, 6 | 4, 5, 6 |
| Blocks | Theme conflicts, speed, uninstall residue | Client support burden, no proof, overlap with Gorgias or Klaviyo | A new program with no record, time away from billable work | Cost without a sales figure, "we already have chat" |
| Drivers | Theme app embed, setup skill, sandbox, paid session | Client-visible Analytics, a credited case study | Paid from the first engagement, a publishable case study | The phrases shoppers asked that found nothing |
| Assets | Setup skill, sandbox, one-pager, walkthrough video | Findings template, sample Analytics, permission form | Partner terms, session scope, the platform-rules note | Findings list, plan page, the merchant breakeven worksheet |
| Channels | LinkedIn by hand, Shopify Developer Community | LinkedIn, cold email | Cold email, LinkedIn, DotDev (to test) | Through the agency only |

## Design partners: the paid usability cohort
Implementers serving US stores, reachable on Upwork, Fiverr, email, or LinkedIn, willing to install Pico on a development store or a permissioned client store, give structured feedback, join an interview, and consider a case study. Current tools: Shopify CLI, the theme editor, development stores, coding agents for some, and the apps agencies list most (Klaviyo, Gorgias, Recharge, Okendo, Rebuy).

Targets: 30 sessions by day 60, median setup under 30 minutes, 15 interviews, 3 case study permissions from both sides, 15 partner sign-ups by day 90.

How it runs: 30 paid sessions in 60 days from week 1 (Upwork 15, Fiverr 5, email 6, LinkedIn 4). Fee $150, paid on the platform where found, or by invoice within 7 days of the completed feedback form, with a session agreement and a W-9 or W-8BEN. Interview optional, 30 minutes, $75. Case studies only with recorded permission from merchant and implementer. The partnership offer is open through email, LinkedIn, and Pico's own pages, never inside Fiverr, and Upwork partners are paid through Upwork for 24 months. Exit at 30 sessions (week 9) or the first permissioned case study, then batches of 10 under the runway gate.

Early adopter traits: has installed AI chat for clients, uses coding agents, replies quickly, willing to be credited in public.


===== reference/icp-personas-merchants.md =====

# ICP and personas, merchants

Load for targeting, segmentation, persona-specific copy, and founding cohort intake. Distills the merchant ICP Dashboard and Buying Committee (2026-11-03). Bands come from `ops/decisions.md` D53 and D54. Counts: `market-sizing.md`.

## The two levels

| | Level 1: no conversational discovery yet | Level 2: started and stalled |
|---|---|---|
| Segment | US Shopify stores whose shoppers need help choosing between similar or technical products, on Shopify's own search, no AI assistant | Growing brands already paying for a search, quiz, or chat app whose shoppers still miss products |
| Categories | Health, sports and outdoor, pets, auto parts and fitment, consumer electronics. Home and garden adjacent | The same, plus home and garden and beauty |
| Bands (planning) | 100+ products, 10,000 to 100,000 sessions a month, 1 to 10 people, about $150,000 to $3 million a year, Basic or Grow | 250+ products, 100,000 to 1 million sessions, 10 to 50 people plus an agency, about $1.5 to $30 million, Advanced or Plus |
| Fit check | 2% of sessions start a conversation: 200 to 2,000 a month, Growth or Pro | 2,000 to 20,000 a month, Pro then Scale, then custom |
| Pain | Shoppers who don't know a product's name leave or email. The owner answers the same questions by hand. Wary of app bills that grow | A paid search or quiz app still leaves requests unmatched. Reports don't show what shoppers asked an assistant. Too many bills |
| Triggers | Repeat pre-purchase questions, a new product line, opening "Searches with no results", peak season prep, a redesign, Shopify AI news | Switching chat apps, a search or quiz app renewal, a replatform, a new market, an agency recommendation |
| Engagement | Self-serve: sandbox, App Store install, checklist, Free, 14 day trial | Agency-installed or assisted onboarding through the founding cohort and implementer partners |

## The buying committee

**Level 1 collapses into one person.** The owner installs, approves the charge in Shopify Billing, and cancels by uninstalling. Blocks: fear of a growing bill, setup time, wrong answers to shoppers, doubt it beats the free Inbox agent, theme risk, no reviews yet. Drivers: fewer repeat questions, shoppers finding products alone, seeing what shoppers ask, no card to start. Buy-in assets: the sandbox, listing screenshots of cards and Analytics, the checklist, a plan page that states each quota, the Shopper Words Test. Channels: App Store search and the AI Shopping Assistants collection, Google and AI answer engines, roundups, Shopify Community, their freelancer, YouTube (to test).

**Level 2 holds, plus the implementer.**

| | User | Manager | Decision maker | Implementer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Titles | Ecommerce manager, merchandiser, CX lead | Head of ecommerce, growth or CRO lead | Founder, CEO, GM | Agency or freelance developer, theme developer |
| Influence | Shortlists, runs the trial | Approves the trial and spend | Signs, can veto | Rarely signs, can block by never enabling the embed |
| Stages | 2 to 5 | 1, 3, 5, 6 | 3, 4, 7 | 3, 4, 7 |
| Blocks | Another dashboard, catalog fix work, clashes with existing apps | No revenue attribution, overlap with paid tools, a vendor with no reviews | Cost without proof of sales, "Shopify's free agent is good enough" | Theme conflicts, speed impact, uninstall residue |
| Drivers | A list of catalog fixes, something to report upward | Evidence for merchandising, fewer tools | A low-risk start, a flat price with a stated quota | No theme code, a setup skill, a sandbox, the partner share |
| Assets | Sandbox, Analytics tour, checklist, the "not offered" list | Trial Analytics, the breakeven worksheet, plan comparison | A one-page summary with the breakeven arithmetic | The setup skill, the technical one-pager, the paid session |

## Design partners: the founding cohort
20 US stores in the five categories, 100+ products, on Basic, Grow, or Advanced, run by someone who opens their own analytics and will install an app with no reviews. They get hands-on onboarding, a direct line to the founder, roadmap input, and 50% off any paid plan for 6 billing periods. They give feedback on setup and Analytics, and permission to cite outcomes only if they agree.

Success metrics, measured by Pico only: widget seen within 24 hours, first conversation within 7 days, 3 catalog fixes from the report in 60 days, and the zero result rate on requests in days 31 to 60 against days 1 to 30 as the store's own baseline. No sales figure is a success metric until revenue attribution exists.

Sources: Shopper Words Test and the Findability Scorecard, the App Store listing, client stores brought by implementer partners. Opens 2026-12-01, closes at 20 stores or 90 days after the listing goes live. Case study request in writing at day 60.

Early adopter traits: tries new apps, answers email, joins a monthly 30-minute call, comfortable being told the product is early.


===== reference/innovation-accounting.md =====

# Innovation accounting: how activity becomes knowledge

Load when logging any activity, reading progress, closing an experiment, or deciding to pivot or persevere. Synthesized for this brain from the compounding loop, the 90-day targets (D44, D45), and the "reopen when" triggers in `ops/decisions.md`.

## The idea
Pico is pre-launch, so the only honest measure of progress is validated learning: which assumptions survived contact with real merchants and implementers, and how fast. Every activity (a session, an install, a review, a call note, a shipped asset) becomes an event. Events roll up into metrics. Metrics test hypotheses. Hypotheses close experiments. Experiments and tripwires reopen or confirm decisions. Decisions change ledgers, and ledgers improve every next asset. That chain is the snowball.

## The three milestones
1. **Baseline.** Measure where each funnel really is. Until day 30 after the listing is live, and until the first 10 paid sessions, every metric is a baseline, not a verdict.
2. **Tune.** Run experiments that move one metric at a time toward its target: listing screenshots, the activation checklist, the first email's opening line, the Upwork post's fee.
3. **Pivot or persevere.** At the day 60 and day 90 reviews, and whenever a tripwire fires, decide with the numbers in `innovation/LEDGER.md`. Write the decision in `ops/decisions.md`, including what it does not change.

## The objects (schemas in `schemas/`)

| Object | Lives in | Written by | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| Event | `innovation/events/YYYY-MM.jsonl`, append only | `tools/brain.py event`, the MCP server, CI, webhooks | One activity, with time, type, audience, data, and references |
| Signal | `ops/signal-log.md`, mirrored as a `signal.logged` event | `tools/brain.py signal` | Raw market input awaiting triage |
| Metric | `innovation/metrics.json` | Edited by hand, reviewed monthly | A KPI: definition, target, comparator, review point, and how it is computed from events |
| Hypothesis | `innovation/hypotheses.json` | Edited by hand | A leap-of-faith assumption with its metric and its pass and fail thresholds |
| Experiment | `innovation/experiments.json` | Edited by hand, closed at its end date | A time-boxed test of a hypothesis, with budget, result, and learning |
| Tripwire | `innovation/tripwires.json` | Edited with the decision it guards | A machine-checkable "reopen when" condition for a decision |
| Ledger | `innovation/LEDGER.md`, generated | `tools/brain.py ledger` | The current state of all of the above, for humans and agents |

## Metric rules
- **Actionable:** every metric names the stage it measures and the decision it informs. No vanity counts like page views without a conversion.
- **Accessible:** every metric is defined in one sentence a merchant could follow.
- **Auditable:** every value traces to events with a source. No number enters the ledger without one.
- Cohorts beat totals. Compare founding stores by install week, and sessions by channel.

## The event taxonomy
`metric.observed`, `signal.logged`, `install`, `activation.step`, `conversation.first`, `plan.changed`, `uninstall`, `review.received`, `session.offered`, `session.completed`, `interview.completed`, `case_study.permission`, `partner.signed`, `payout.made`, `asset.shipped`, `experiment.started`, `experiment.closed`, `decision.made`, `decision.reopened`, `milestone`. Unknown types are allowed but warned, so the taxonomy can grow without breaking the log.

## How the snowball compounds
- Every signal is kept verbatim, so customer language accumulates in `ops/copy-bank.md`.
- Every closed experiment leaves a learning that later prompts can cite.
- Every tripwire check is a recorded "nothing changed" or a dated reopen, so decisions stay settled until evidence moves them.
- Every amendment improves every future asset, for every operator and every agent, without anyone being told.

## Weekly loop (Monday)
1. Pull metrics: add `metric.observed` events for each KPI with new data.
2. Triage signals in `ops/signal-log.md`.
3. Run `python3 tools/brain.py tripwires` and `python3 tools/brain.py ledger`.
4. Close or start experiments. Route any AMEND through the procedure.

## Never
Never backfill an event with an estimate. Never edit or delete a past event: append a correction with `refs` to the original. Never let a metric value reach copy: metrics are internal until they enter the proof log with permission.


===== reference/launch-plan.md =====

# Launch plan: calendar, build list, budget

Load for anything date-bound: what ships when, what a given week is for, and what money is released. Distills the launch calendar and D31, D32, D56. Week 1 starts Monday 2026-11-09. Black Friday is 2026-11-27 and Cyber Monday 2026-11-30, when US stores freeze theme changes.

## The calendar

| Week | Starts | What happens | Decisions |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2026-11-09 | Site aligned. Listing submitted. Speed test on Dawn. Inventory webhook live. US mailbox registered. First Upwork post, first emails and LinkedIn messages | D2, D3, D18, D19, D37, D47, D56 |
| 2 | 2026-11-16 | First paid sessions on development stores. Terms clause and permission forms ready. Sync failure email live. Both scorecards tested with five implementers and five client merchants | D33, D51, D56 |
| 3 | 2026-11-23 | Listing live target. Merchant scorecard live. Outreach pauses from Wednesday for Thanksgiving | D2 |
| 4 | 2026-11-30 | First insight email and weekly summary live. Founding cohort opens 2026-12-01 | D30, D56 |
| 5 | 2026-12-07 | Counsel review of the partner terms | D50 |
| 6 | 2026-12-14 | Partner ledger, payout run, proof capture point live. Partner page and implementer scorecard live. Invitations to participants met by email and LinkedIn | D35 to D40, D49, D56 |
| 8 | 2026-12-28 | Monthly usage summary live | D56 |
| 9 | 2027-01-04 | 30 sessions complete. First case study permission requests | D37, D45 |
| 10 | 2027-01-11 | The words against the catalog check goes live as a public page | D56 |
| 12 | 2027-01-25 | Day 60 review of the founding cohort and both target sets | D44, D45 |
| 13 | 2027-02-01 | Day 90 review. The next spend block is released, or not | D31, D32 |

The listing has a buffer to week 6. Until it is live, every merchant CTA is "Connect your store" on picofinds.com, and implementer sessions run on development stores, which need no approved listing.

## The 90-day cash budget, $9,000, capped at $3,000 a month

| Line | Amount |
|---|---|
| 15 paid sessions on Upwork, about $177 each | $2,655 |
| 5 paid sessions on Fiverr, about $162 each | $809 |
| 10 paid sessions by invoice, about $152 each | $1,520 |
| 15 interviews, about $81 each | $1,215 |
| ScoreApp Starter, 3 months | $117 |
| LinkedIn Sales Navigator Core, 3 months | $360 |
| Email sending domain and inboxes | $90 |
| US private mailbox for the CAN-SPAM address | $90 |
| Counsel review of the partner terms | $1,000 |
| Held back | $1,144 |

## The runway gate
Spend is released in 30-day blocks. Each block needs at least 6 months of company runway after it. If a block fails, paid sessions pause and outreach continues on email, LinkedIn, and the scorecard.

## Slip rule
If any build list item slips by more than two weeks, the founder and engineer move the next block's scope, and the change is a decision entry.

## Feedback cadence
Founding merchants: a monthly 30-minute call. Partners: a quarterly call and a findings digest after each batch of 10 sessions.


===== reference/lead-magnets.md =====

# Lead magnets, both audiences

Load to build, edit, or reply to anything around the two ScoreApp scorecards. Distills both lead magnet specifications and scorecard briefs (2026-11-03). Every result message says the score is a self-assessment. No industry statistic is quoted.

## Shopify Store Findability Scorecard (merchants, live week 3)

**Reveals** whether shoppers who describe a product in their own words are likely to find it: catalog size and likeness, the words in product titles, how pre-purchase questions arrive, and whether the merchant can see what shoppers asked.

**Seven questions, 100 points, higher means more findability risk:** products sold (0 to 15), how alike they are (0 to 15), what shoppers ask before buying (0 to 15), whether they read "Searches with no results" in Shopify's search analytics (0 to 15), whether titles use shoppers' words (0 to 15), how shoppers without the product name find it (3 to 15), whether they can see what shoppers asked (0 to 10).

| Score | Tier | CTA |
|---|---|---|
| 0 to 39 | Shoppers can find their way | Get the Shopper Words Test worksheet |
| 40 to 69 | Some shoppers may be getting lost | Try your phrases in the Pico sandbox store |
| 70 to 100 | Shoppers ask in words your catalog doesn't use | Install Pico free, or apply for the founding cohort |

**Landing page.** Headline: "How easily can shoppers find your products in their own words?" Subhead: "Seven questions, a score from 0 to 100, and three fixes you can make this week." CTA: "Get my Findability Score". Footer: "Your score is your own assessment, based on your answers. It is not a measurement of your store."

**Emails, plain text, one CTA, 60 words or fewer:** day 0 the score and three fixes, day 2 ten phrases with a labeled sandbox example, day 5 what Pico does and does not do, day 8 the founding cohort, which closes at 20 stores or 90 days after the listing is live. No invented deadline.

**Routing.** 70 to 100 goes to the founder for the founding cohort. Tag by tier and by answers to questions 3 and 7.

## Agency AI Shopping Readiness Scorecard (implementers, live week 6)

**Reveals** whether the implementer has a tested, maintainable answer when clients ask for AI shopping help: setup without theme edits, something to show the client, and a way to be paid for evaluation time.

**Seven questions on stack, client base, and AI work, higher means a bigger readiness gap** and a stronger fit for the paid session. Question 1 counts client stores set up or maintained in a year.

**Path.** Score, three next steps, the Client Store Findability Audit template, the sandbox and setup skill, an application for a paid session, then a case study and the partnership.

**Landing page.** Headline: "When a client asks for AI shopping help, how ready is your answer?" Subhead: "Seven questions for Shopify developers and agencies, a score from 0 to 100, and three next steps." CTA: "Get my readiness score".

**Emails:** day 0 the score and next steps, day 2 what a zero result phrase tells a client, day 5 paid to test it on a store you work on, day 8 the session cohort and the partner program, sent by email only.

## Shared rules
- CAN-SPAM in every email: a working unsubscribe and a postal address.
- Source and campaign parameters on every link, so stage 1 KPIs can be counted.
- No Arabic or GCC version now.
- Implementer scorecard emails never go inside Upwork or Fiverr.

# Market sizing, both audiences

Load for board, investor, or planning questions about how big each segment is. These are frames, not market sizes. Each figure keeps its own source, method, and date, and figures from different trackers are never added together. Never quote a sizing number in customer copy.

## Merchants (StoreLeads, which counts stores it detects as live and selling)

| Lens | Figure | Method | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live US Shopify stores | 1,253,193 | StoreLeads US page | 2026-10-30 |

**Reading it.** Level 1 is large and unproven. Level 2 is smaller and easier to find, because stores already paying for search or chat are visible through install trackers. Both sit beside a free native agent on about 358,000 stores.
