===== reference/marketing-campaigns.md =====

# Marketing campaigns and asset backlog

Load to plan, prioritize, or produce an asset. Distills both Assets and Collaterals Libraries (2026-11-03). Each audience runs three channels, and its demand driver is the top-of-funnel asset in every one. Timeframes are production estimates for a two-person team.

## Merchants

**Shopify App Store.** Where merchants search, compare, and install.
- TOFU: Shopper Words Test as listing screenshots (request, cards, clarifying question, Analytics), 1 week. Listing copy and category placement: "Pico AI Shopping Assistant" in Chat, 3 days.
- MOFU: pricing section and demo store link, every quota and the conversation definition beside the prices, 2 days.
- BOFU: review request after value realization, a reply to every review within 2 business days, no incentives, 1 week.

**Content and search, including AI answer engines.**
- TOFU: Shopper Words Test as a worksheet and guide, 1 week. Catalog and search guides for the five categories, 2 weeks.
- MOFU: comparison and alternative pages, every fact page-loaded, sourced, dated, rechecked, 2 weeks. Answer engine pages: how Pico works, FAQ, what Pico does not do, 1 week.
- BOFU: pricing page with the breakeven worksheet, inputs blank for the merchant, 1 week. Technical one-pager, 3 days, shared with implementers.

**Product-led lifecycle.**
- TOFU: Shopper Words Test as a guided sandbox tour with suggested requests, 1 week.
- MOFU: activation checklist prompts and setup emails, 2 weeks. First insight email, live week 4.
- BOFU: trial to paid sequence, no false urgency, 1 week. Cancel flow with reason and retention offer, exists.

## Implementers

**Cold email to US implementers.**
- TOFU: the Paid Usability Session offer, plain text under 120 words, 3 days. Agency AI Shopping Readiness Scorecard link in a second email, 1 week.
- MOFU: sandbox and setup follow-up with the setup skill and one-pager, 3 days. Session brief and client permission template, 1 week.
- BOFU: case study permission and partnership offer, email only, 1 week.

**LinkedIn outreach, by hand.**
- TOFU: connection note and first message with the paid session, 2 days. Founder posts on method: theme app embed, setup by coding agent, what a zero result phrase means, 1 day each.
- MOFU: setup walkthrough video on a development store, uninstall shown, 1 week.
- BOFU: partnership invitation message with the partner page, from week 6, 2 days.

**Upwork and Fiverr job posts.**
- TOFU: Upwork fixed-price job post for the session, $150, 2 days. Fiverr order of an existing app setup gig or a posted brief, 2 days.
- MOFU: session kit inside the platform: brief, sandbox link, setup skill link, feedback form, 2 days.
- BOFU: an honest platform review and an optional $75 interview as a second milestone or order, 1 day.

## Held back, and why
- Paid ads: an unproven offer with no conversion data buys expensive evidence. Revisit once the listing converts.
- Cold outbound to store owners: with an empty proof log, a cold message can only describe features.
- LinkedIn automation and LinkedIn Ads: barred by LinkedIn's User Agreement, and replaced by marketplace posts.
- A partner pitch inside Upwork or Fiverr: platform rules. The partner page is public.
- GCC and Arabic-market assets, and Gulf agency outreach: for later, on the trigger in `gcc-later.md`.

## Production rules for every asset
Claims in narrowed wording only. Sample data labeled as sample. No competitor named. Shopify never disparaged. One call to action. Run `ops/QA-checklist.md`, then list the asset in `ops/asset-index.md` and log an `asset.shipped` event.


===== reference/objection-handling.md =====

# Objection handling

Load for sales calls, partner calls, review replies, support macros, and FAQ pages. Derived from the buying committee blockers, the competitive weaknesses, and the claim ledger. Headings are in the buyer's words. Where the honest answer is "not yet", it says not yet.

## Merchants

**"Why not just turn on Shopify's free Inbox agent?"**
You can, and it is free. Pico costs more. The reason to install is what you learn: the phrases your shoppers asked that returned nothing or drew few clicks. Try it in the sandbox, then on the Free plan, before paying anything.

**"Will it tell my shoppers something wrong?"**
Product cards show names, prices, and stock from your synced catalog, and the Catalog page shows the last successful sync. The AI writes the reply text, so read a few conversations in your first week. Stock is as of your last sync.

**"Will it break my theme or slow my store?"**
Pico runs as a theme app embed called Pico Assistant, so there is no theme code to edit, and Shopify removes embed blocks on uninstall. The speed test on Dawn is being measured now, and the number will be on the technical one-pager. We do not claim zero impact.

**"What happens when I hit the quota? I've been burned by app bills."**
Today the Plan & Usage page shows a quota meter. Coming soon: alerts at 80% and 100%, a 10% grace allowance on paid plans, then a pause until the next cycle or an upgrade. No overage charge, ever. A conversation is a thread with at least one AI reply, counted once per shopper and device per 24 hours.

**"Does it increase sales?"**
Pico does not measure revenue yet, and the dashboard says so. It measures what shoppers asked, what they were shown, what they clicked, and what they added to cart. Revenue attribution is on the roadmap.

**"Can it answer order and returns questions, or hand off to my team?"**
No. Pico answers product questions before purchase. Keep your help desk for orders and people.

**"You have no reviews."**
Correct, Pico is new. That is why the sandbox exists and why the Free plan includes every feature, so you can check every claim yourself. The founding cohort gets hands-on onboarding and a direct line to the founder.

**"Is it semantic search?"**
No. An AI model reads the request, then Pico matches it to your catalog by keywords, synonyms, and price range. If a request uses words your catalog doesn't, it shows up as a zero result phrase, which is the point of the report.

## Implementers

**"Is the $150 real, and when do I get paid?"**
Yes. The session brief states scope, fee, and payment route before you accept. On Upwork it is a fixed-price milestone, on Fiverr an order, otherwise an invoice paid within 7 days of the completed feedback form.

**"Will this break my client's store?"**
Start in the sandbox or on a development store. On a client store, the merchant agrees in writing first. Install is a theme app embed, removed on uninstall.

**"Your partner program has no track record."**
True. The terms are decided and published on picofinds.com/partners from week 6: 25% of each referred store's subscription for 24 months, 30% at five active paying stores, payouts on the 15th. No partner has been paid yet, so watch the first payout.

**"Why should I move my client off Gorgias or Klaviyo?"**
You shouldn't. Pico does product discovery before purchase, beside their stack. Show the client the phrases their shoppers asked that found nothing, and let them decide.

**"Can you guarantee me leads?"**
No. Merchants who ask Pico for setup help are offered listed partners in rotation, and you see the count each month. No volume is promised.

**"Do I need one login per client?"**
Today, yes: each plan connects one store, and you take the admin role on each client's account. A multi-store workspace is built once 10 partners each have 3 or more active paying stores.

**"Can I white label it?"**
No. There is no white label or resale.


===== reference/outreach-engine.md =====

# Channel engine, implementers: cold email, LinkedIn, Upwork and Fiverr

Load first for any implementer outreach: emails, LinkedIn notes and posts, job posts, session kits, partner invitations. Synthesized from the implementer journey, assets library, platform rules research, and decisions D33 to D52.

## Thesis
Every message is an offer of paid work, not a pitch: $150 for up to 90 minutes on a store the implementer already works on. Freelancers already sell app installs for about $100, so a paid session reads as ordinary work. The partnership follows the session, never leads it.

## How the channels feed each other
Upwork brings applicants to a posted job (15 sessions). Fiverr starts from an existing gig or a brief (5). Cold email (6) and LinkedIn (4) reach agencies that do not sell on marketplaces. Every session produces findings for the client, an interview, a possible case study, and from week 6 a partner who joined through Pico's own pages.

## Platform rules, load-bearing
- **Cold email (CAN-SPAM):** accurate headers and subject, identified as an advertisement, the US postal address, an opt-out honored within 10 business days. US recipients only in the first 90 days. Then UK companies and LLPs only, never UK sole traders or ordinary partnerships, never cold to the EU.
- **LinkedIn:** messages sent by hand. No bots, no automation, no scraping tools.
- **Upwork:** relationships found there keep payments on Upwork for 24 months unless a conversion fee is paid. Partners met there are paid through Upwork for 24 months.
- **Fiverr:** payment only by a Fiverr order. No outside link meant to move the relationship, no email request, no partner invitation.
- Counsel reviews the partner terms, session brief, and conduct rules in week 5.

## Archetypes
- **The paid offer.** Scope and fee in the first line, deliverables, reply to book.
- **The method post.** One idea: install through a theme app embed, setup by coding agent, what a zero result phrase means.
- **The walkthrough.** A real recording on a development store, uninstall shown.
- **The findings handoff.** What the client's shoppers asked that found nothing, as a list the implementer can bill fixes against.
- **The invitation.** After a session: case study permission, then the partner terms quoted exactly.

## Plan, write, edit
1. **Plan.** One level (freelancer or agency), one stage, one channel, its platform rule.
2. **Write.** Under 120 words for a first email. Fee and scope first. Lines from `ops/copy-bank.md`.
3. **Edit.** Strip any income, traffic, certification, or white label language. Check the channel rule line by line.

## Calls to action
"Apply for a paid session." "Download the setup skill." "Read the technical one-pager." From week 6, off-platform only: "Read the terms on Pico's partner page."

## What good looks like
Cold email reply rate 5%, above the 3.43% average a 2026 report cites. LinkedIn acceptance 30%, replies from 15%. 10 qualified applicants per Upwork post, or the fee rises to $200. 30 sessions by day 60. Payment within 7 days of the feedback form, every time.

## Never in this channel
Automated LinkedIn sends, purchased lists used outside their terms, partner pitches inside Upwork or Fiverr, rates other than the published terms, named prospects in reports, Gulf agency outreach.


===== reference/partner-program.md =====

# Partner program and implementer economics

Load for anything about paying implementers: session fees, the partner share, tiers, payouts, attribution, and partner FAQs. Distills the implementer Pricing and Packaging dashboard and D33 to D41. Everything here is IN BUILD: sessions from week 2, the partner page in week 6.

## What Pico pays for

| Element | Terms |
|---|---|
| Paid Usability Session | $150 for a fixed scope of up to 90 minutes. Pico pays the platform fees |
| Interview | $75 for 30 minutes, optional, after the session |
| Referred store share | 25% of the store's subscription charges for 24 months from its first paid charge |
| Lead partner share | 30% on referred stores from the month the partner reaches 5 active paying stores |
| Managed share | 10% on stores the partner manages but did not refer |
| One share per store | No stacking. No cash bounty, no resale margin, no client discount at launch |

## The ladder

| Tier | Entry | Pays | Also gets | Target |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Session participant | A completed paid session | $150, plus $75 for an interview | A partner invitation, a case study offer | 30 sessions by day 60 |
| Partner | An accepted application, open to anyone who completed a session or runs one active client store | 25% referred, 10% managed | A listing on picofinds.com/partners after the first active paying store, free development store testing | 15 partners by day 90 |
| Lead partner | 5 active paying stores, referred or managed | 30% referred, 10% managed | Co-marketing, a published case study, a tier badge, priority support | 3 by month 6 |
| Agency workspace | A partner with 3 or more active client stores | Free to the partner, each store pays its own plan | One workspace across client stores | Built when 10 partners qualify |

Good standing: at least one active paying store in the last 12 months, no platform rule breach, no incentivized reviews, copy that uses the narrowed claims. Earned shares continue to term unless a partner is removed for a breach.

## Payouts
Monthly on the 15th, for subscription charges Shopify paid out to Pico in the prior month. $50 minimum, carried forward. PayPal or bank transfer. Tax forms before the first payout. A ledger until 25 partners, then a partner platform. Partners met on Upwork are paid through Upwork for the first 24 months.

## Attribution
Deal registration: the partner registers the client store's myshopify domain before the install, the merchant confirms by email, and the first valid registration holds for 90 days. Checked against install and charge records in the Partner Dashboard.

## Referral traffic
Merchants who ask Pico for setup help, through "Book a tailored demo" or support, are offered a listed partner, in rotation and by country. Partners see the count each month. No volume is promised.

## The economics, internal
- One paid session costs about $177 on Upwork, $162 on Fiverr, $152 by invoice.
- One referred Growth store kept a year returns about $441 to Pico after a 25% share, before model cost, so it pays for about 2.5 Upwork sessions. After model cost at the ceiling, about 1.7.
- What implementers earn now: about $100 per AI chat app install. Pico: $150 for the first session, then 25% of the plan, $12.25 a month on Growth, $294 over 24 months, if the client keeps paying.
- Benchmarks, structure only: Gorgias 20% for 2 to 3 years, Rebuy 5% to 15% for 12 months plus 5% managed, Okendo 20%, Octane 20% for life, Shopify 20% of the merchant's subscription.

## Never say
"Earn recurring revenue", "guaranteed leads", "certified partner", "white label", any rate other than the published terms, or "Join the Pico Partner Program" before the page is live.


===== reference/positioning-verdict.md =====

# Positioning verdicts, the settled forks

Load when someone asks why Pico leads on what it leads on, or proposes leading on something else. Distills the two positioning summaries and the competitive vectors, 2026-11-03.

## Merchants: shopper insight over support automation

**Verdict.** Pico positions on insight into what shoppers ask and on answers traceable to the synced catalog. It does not compete on support automation breadth, where AI sales and support agents lead.

**Why.** Those are the two vectors where the slate scores lowest. The first conversation with a merchant changes from "trust our lift number" to "see what your shoppers asked for", which the merchant can check in the sandbox and then on their own store on the free plan. It answers the complaints reviewers repeat after billing surprises: answers they cannot check, and results they never see. Every install is a choice against a free native agent on about 358,000 stores, so Pico wins on what the merchant learns, not on what the assistant can do.

| Vector | Leader | Pico now, target | Edge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Easy setup with responsive help | Chatty 8.9 | 6.8, 7.9 | Competitors |
| Support automation breadth | Tidio 8.9 | 1.3, 1.3 by design | Competitors |
| Insight into what shoppers ask | Pico 8.3 | 8.3, 9.1 | Pico |
| Answers traceable to the catalog | Pico 7.7, Search & Discovery 7.1 | 7.7, 8.4 | Pico, narrowly |

**Defensibility.** Narrow and copyable: Shopify reports search-bar zero results, and Tidio lists questions Lyro could not answer, so a conversational report is one release away for either. The defensible part is the loop after the report: each zero result phrase becomes a catalog fix, and Pico shows whether the fix worked (holdout measurement, the proof capture point), plus the request history each store builds. If Pico ships that loop first and implementers adopt it as their audit tool, the lead compounds. If it stays a report, it is a feature, and it will be matched.

**What moves the targets.** Setup: hands-on founding cohort onboarding and implementers installing for stores. Insight: holdout measurement and the proof capture point. Traceability: showing in Analytics which catalog products each answer used.

## Implementers: paid first over partner economics

**Verdict.** Pico positions on paying implementers from the first engagement and on proof the implementer co-owns. It does not compete on established partner economics or stack presence, where the programs agencies already know lead.

**Why.** Every program on the slate pays after a referral or a closed deal. Paying for a usability session on first contact turns cold email, LinkedIn messages, and marketplace job posts into offers of paid work rather than pitches, which fits how freelancers already sell: app installs for about $100, research sessions benchmarked at $100 to $150 an hour. One partner serves 2 to 10 client stores as a freelancer, 10 to 100 as an agency (planning bands), so one partner can mean repeat deployments.

| Vector | Leader | Pico now, target | Edge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Established partner economics | Shopify Partner Program 9.1 | 0.4, 4.6 | Competitors |
| Presence in the stack agencies sell | Klaviyo 9.3 | 0.2, 2.1 | Competitors |
| Paid from the first engagement | Build 6.9 | 0.0, 8.8 | Pico, by design |
| Proof the implementer co-owns | Build 6.8 | 1.1, 8.3 | Pico, by design |

**Defensibility.** Paying for sessions is easy to copy. What compounds is what sessions produce: case studies owned jointly and gated by permission, and implementers who have put Pico on several client stores, which needs the multi-store workspace once 10 partners each have 3 or more active stores. The gap between the first session and the partnership must close fast, because Gorgias, Klaviyo, and the Shopify Partner Program set the floor: a share, a tier, a directory. Upwork's 24-month term and Fiverr's off-platform ban mean the program must be joinable through email, LinkedIn, and Pico's own pages.

## Decided around both verdicts
- Two standalone go-to-markets, never blended in one asset.
- USA first, the GCC on a trigger (`gcc-later.md`).
- Open proof until the proof log has its first entry.
- A slate competitor shipping a conversational zero-result report reopens the merchant verdict's wording, not its direction: lead with the fix loop.


===== reference/positioning.md =====

# Positioning statements, both audiences

Load for any headline, tagline, page hero, or pitch. Distills the two positioning dashboards (Dashboard 3 per audience, 2026-11-03).

## Merchants

**Core claim.** Pico shows merchants what their shoppers ask for, and answers shoppers with products drawn from the store's own synced catalog.

**1. Against AI sales chat and support agents.** Not "another AI chatbot that tries to answer everything", a shopping assistant built around your synced catalog that shows you what shoppers asked for. Shoppers describe what they need in their own words, and Pico replies with product cards showing names, prices, and stock from the synced catalog. The merchant sees what shoppers asked for, what they clicked and added to cart, and the phrases that returned no products or few clicks.
- Basis: support automation breadth is where agents lead (vector 2), insight into what shoppers ask is where the slate scores lowest (vector 3).
- Must not drift into: "never makes things up", "the only assistant that sticks to your catalog", "increases sales".

**2. Against search, quiz, and recommendation tools, and custom builds.** Not "a smarter search bar", a conversation for shoppers who don't know a product's name. Search, filters, quizzes, and widgets stay where they are. Pico adds a place to describe the need, one clarifying question when a request is vague, product cards from the synced catalog, and one tap to the store's own cart. It installs from the App Store with a four-step checklist.
- Basis: Pico has no semantic search, filters, or recommendation widgets, so it sits beside search.
- Must not drift into: any comparison with Shopify search, "understands what shoppers mean", "semantic search", "checkout in chat", "no developer needed".

**3. Against doing nothing.** Not "one more app to manage", a low-risk way to see what your shoppers are asking for. The theme, search, and collections stay. Pico adds a widget through a theme app embed, with no theme code to edit. Try the sandbox first, then start on Free, 50 conversations a month, with a 14 day Growth trial and no card.
- Must not drift into: "free forever", "unlimited", "zero setup", "your store is losing sales".

## Implementers

**Core claim.** Pico pays implementers for a first session on a store they work on, and, with the client's permission, credits their work in the case study that follows.

**1. Against AI assistant vendors with agency programs.** Not "another affiliate program that pays after the referral", a paid session that starts before any referral exists. We pay you $150 to install Pico on a store you work on and tell us what works and what breaks. With your client's written permission, we write up what changed on their store and credit your work. Participants are invited to the partner program: 25% of each referred store's subscription for 24 months.
- Basis: every program found pays after a referral or a closed deal (vector 3), and none credits the implementer as a standard element (vector 4).
- Must not drift into: "earn recurring revenue", "join the Pico Partner Program", "certified partner", "white label", "guaranteed leads".

**2. Against custom builds, the free native agent, and the standard stack.** Not "a build you have to maintain", an app you set up in four steps or hand to your coding agent. Pico installs through a theme app embed, and Shopify removes app embed blocks on uninstall. The client gets an Analytics page listing the phrases shoppers asked that returned no products or few clicks.
- Must not drift into: "installs itself", "zero setup", any speed claim beyond the published Lighthouse result, anything about what the native agent lacks.

**3. Against offering no AI shopping help.** Not "a new service line to build from scratch", a paid first session on a store you already work on. Try the sandbox first, then run a paid session and leave with the phrases its shoppers asked that the catalog could not answer.
- Basis: no AI shopping assistant appears on 26 sampled agency stack pages, and freelancers already sell app installs for about $100.
- Must not drift into: "a new revenue stream", "your clients will sell more".

## What would change these statements
- Revenue attribution or holdout measurement ships and produces data: an outcome line becomes possible, only after it enters the proof log.
- Human handoff ships: the "tries to answer everything" contrast weakens.
- A slate competitor ships a conversational zero-result report: lead with the fix loop in `positioning-verdict.md`.
- The partner terms change, or the multi-store workspace ships: implementer statements quote the new terms.
- The first case study has recorded permission: a proof line in its exact permitted wording.

GCC variant, for later only: `gcc-later.md`.


===== reference/pricing-and-packaging.md =====

# Pricing and packaging, merchants

Load for plan questions, pricing pages, upgrade prompts, and ROI conversations. Distills the merchant Pricing and Packaging dashboard and D21 to D29. Status of each element is in `rules/feature-status.md`. ROI inputs about Pico's effect are always left blank for the merchant.

## The value metric
Per conversation, which holds. It matches what Pico does and measures, matches the unit Chatty and Tidio Lyro use, and the merchant can watch it on the quota meter. Secondary metric: stores per plan, one store each.

A conversation is a chat thread that gets at least one AI reply. Messages from the same shopper on the same device within 24 hours belong to the same conversation. Fair use: up to 50 AI replies per conversation.

Rejected denominators: per visitor (charges for traffic that never asks), per resolution and commission (need outcome measurement Pico lacks and would invite banned claims), per AI reply (the shopper controls the length), per seat (value lives in shopper conversations).

## The tiers

| Plan | Monthly | Yearly | Conversations | Position | Month 6 target share |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | | 50 | Entry, where every trial lands | 60% of active installs |
| Growth | $49 | $490 (IN BUILD) | 600 | Hero | 70% of paying stores |
| Pro | $99 | $990 (IN BUILD) | 2,000 | Hero+ | 22% |
| Scale (IN BUILD) | $299 | $2,990 | 6,000, plus a 30-minute onboarding call | Anchor | 8% |
| Custom | About $0.05 a conversation | | By request | Off the plan page | |

14 day Growth trial with no card. Every feature on every plan. One store per plan. Charges in USD through Shopify Billing for App Store installs. Founding cohort: 50% off any paid plan for 6 billing periods.

## At the quota (IN BUILD)
Alerts at 80% and 100% in the dashboard and by email. Open conversations finish. Paid plans get a 10% grace allowance at no charge, then the launcher pauses until the next cycle or an upgrade, which applies at once. No overage charge, ever.

## Findings that shape copy
- Growth to Pro is 2.0 times the price for 3.3 times the conversations, a clear upgrade past 600.
- Pico's price per conversation sits below every per-conversation vendor sampled. Internal input only.
- Shopify's revenue share is 0% on the first $1M of lifetime app revenue, so net price equals list price until then.
- At the $0.02 model cost ceiling, gross margin before other costs is 76% on Growth and 60% on Pro and Scale. Free costs about $1 a month per store in model use.

## Expansion levers
Conversation quota (prompted at 80%), stores (one plan each), billing period (yearly, two months free). Capability by tier: none, by design.

## ROI anchors, always completed by the merchant
- **Cost of the problem:** monthly searches with no results × the share who would have bought × average order margin, all the merchant's own numbers. Plus hours a week answering questions by hand × the cost of an hour (US customer service median $21.53, BLS, May 2025).
- **Alternatives, not like for like:** Growth equals about 2.3 hours of a US service rep. The free Inbox agent costs nothing, so the case rests on what the merchant learns, not on price.
- **Breakeven:** extra orders a month equal to the plan price divided by the merchant's average order margin. Example input only: at a $30 margin, Growth needs 2 orders a month.

Never state a typical customer value, a payback period, or a multiple for Pico. A formula with a blank is honest. A filled-in example is an income claim.

## Calculator
Inputs: average order margin, searches with no results a month, share who would buy, hours a week, cost of an hour. Outputs: breakeven orders per plan, years of Growth covered by one order, margin at stake, cost of answering by hand. The workbook lives in the build repo's Google folder.


===== reference/value-proposition-implementers.md =====

# Value proposition, implementers

Load for any implementer email, LinkedIn message, job post, partner page, or one-pager. Distills the implementer Value Proposition Framework (2026-11-03). Body copy is 25 words or fewer. Proof headlines are open proof.

**Brand promise.** We pay you to try Pico on a store you work on, and we credit your work when your client agrees.

**Positioning.** An AI shopping assistant built for the people who set up stores: a sandbox and a setup skill that cut setup hours, an Analytics page the client can see, a paid first session, and case studies credited to the implementer.

## Pillar 1. Set up without touching theme code
Personas: developer (Level 2), freelancer or studio lead (Level 1).

| RTB | Headline | Emotional | Proof to check | Body (25 words max) | CTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Theme app embed | Install without editing theme code | Nothing left behind on your client's theme | Read Shopify's own docs on app embeds before you install | Pico runs as a theme app embed, so you switch it on in the theme editor instead of editing code. Uninstalling removes the embed block. | Read the technical one-pager |
| Setup skill | Hand setup to your coding agent | Set it up in the tools you already use | Read the setup skill before your agent runs it | Download Pico's setup skill, point your coding agent at a store you work on, and it follows the install and dashboard steps for you. | Download the setup skill |
| Sandbox store | Test it before any client store | No risk to a client's live store | Open the sandbox now, with no client store and no plan | Try the shopper flow on Pico's sandbox store, a sample outdoor gear catalog on the real API. No client store and no plan needed. | Open the sandbox store |

## Pillar 2. Show your client what shoppers ask
Personas: project or account lead (Level 2), freelancer, and the merchant client they report to.

| RTB | Headline | Emotional | Proof to check | Body (25 words max) | CTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Phrases that found nothing | Show clients what their shoppers couldn't find | Bring your client their shoppers' own words | Show a client the phrases on the free plan | Pico lists the phrases your client's shoppers asked that returned no products or few clicks. Each can become a fix you propose. | Run the Shopper Words Test on a client store |
| Roles | Give each person the access they need | Your client stays in charge of their store | Invite your client with the role they need | Add your client and your team with the role each needs: owner, admin, analyst, or support. | Read the technical one-pager |
| Overview | A month-on-month view for your client report | Know the assistant is healthy before your client asks | Put the Overview on your next client call | Open the Overview before a client call: conversations, product click-through rate, and add to cart rate against the previous 30 days, plus sync health. | Run a paid session on a store you work on |

## Pillar 3. Get paid to shape it
Personas: freelancer or studio lead (Level 1), agency owner (Level 2).

| RTB | Headline | Emotional | Proof to check | Body (25 words max) | CTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Paid usability session | Paid to test Pico on a store you work on | Your time is paid for from the first session | $150 for up to 90 minutes, paid within 7 days of your feedback form | We pay you $150 to install Pico on a store you work on, run the Shopper Words Test, and report what works and breaks. | Apply for a paid session |
| Case study credit | A case study that credits your work | Proof you can show your next client | Read the permission form your client would sign | With your client's written permission, we write up what changed on their store and credit your work, so you both have something to show. | Ask about a case study |
| `[IN BUILD, week 6]` Partner program | 25% of each referred store's subscription, for 24 months | Paid while your client keeps paying | Read the full terms before you refer anyone | Session participants are invited to the partner program: 25% of each referred store's subscription for 24 months, 30% at five active stores. | Read the terms on Pico's partner page |

## Supporting proof points (open proof)
- Shopify's developer documentation explains theme app embeds and what happens to app blocks on uninstall.
- The setup skill is a downloadable file. Read every step before you point Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity at a store.
- The Sandbox link in picofinds.com's top menu runs a sample outdoor gear catalog, with a demo widget included.
- The Analytics page is on every plan, Free included, so zero result phrases can be shown to a client before anyone pays.
- The session brief states scope, fee, and payment route before you accept: a fixed-price milestone on Upwork, an order on Fiverr, or an invoice paid within 7 days.
- The merchant and implementer permission forms go out with the session brief, so both sides see the exact wording first.
- `[IN BUILD, week 6]` picofinds.com/partners publishes the share, the 24-month term, the payout date, the $50 minimum, and the rules for good standing.

## Platform rule
Pillar 3, reason 3, the partner program, is used only on Pico's own pages, in email, and on LinkedIn. Never inside Upwork or Fiverr.


===== reference/value-proposition-merchants.md =====

# Value proposition, merchants

Load for any merchant headline, listing copy, landing page, email, or in-product string. Distills the merchant Value Proposition Framework (2026-11-03): promise, three pillars, nine reasons to believe, each with approved copy. Body copy is 25 words or fewer. Proof headlines are open proof: an invitation to check, never a customer result.

**Brand promise.** Shoppers find products from your catalog by asking in their own words, and you see what they asked for.

**Positioning.** Built around your synced catalog, with insight into what shoppers ask. Stated as what Pico is built around, never as something only Pico can do.

## Pillar 1. Shoppers ask in their own words
Personas: store owner (Level 1), ecommerce manager and head of ecommerce (Level 2).

| RTB | Headline | Emotional | Proof to check | Body (25 words max) | CTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Matched to your catalog | Let shoppers describe what they need | For shoppers who don't know the product's name | Ask the sandbox in your own words, then check what it matched | A shopper types "waterproof hiking boots under $150." Pico matches the request to your synced catalog by keywords, synonyms, and price, and shows product cards. | Try it in the sandbox store |
| Cards you can check | Every card comes from your synced catalog | Answers you can check at a glance | Open any card and check it against the catalog | Product cards show the name, image, price, and stock label from your synced catalog. The Catalog page shows your last successful sync. | See the cards in the sandbox store |
| Question to cart | From question to cart in one tap | Vague requests get a question, not a guess | Give the sandbox a vague request and see what it asks | When a request is too vague, Pico asks one clarifying question. Then one tap adds an in-stock variant to your store's cart. | Try a vague request in the sandbox |

## Pillar 2. See what your shoppers asked for
Personas: store owner, head of ecommerce, CRO lead.

| RTB | Headline | Emotional | Proof to check | Body (25 words max) | CTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Discovery funnel | See where requests stop between question and cart | Know what happens after a shopper asks | The Analytics page comes with every plan, Free included | See how many requests returned products, how many got clicks, and how many reached the cart, plus the phrases shoppers used most. | Open the Analytics page in the sandbox |
| Requests that found nothing | See the requests that found nothing | Find out what shoppers looked for and missed | Run the Shopper Words Test on your own product titles | Pico lists the phrases shoppers asked that returned no products or few clicks. Each can point to a gap in your catalog or your descriptions. | Run the Shopper Words Test |
| Overview | Your last 30 days against the 30 before | Know at a glance whether shoppers find things | Sync health and shopper activity on one page from day one | The Overview compares conversations, product click-through rate, and add to cart rate with the previous 30 days, and shows integration and sync health. | See the Overview in the sandbox |

## Pillar 3. A low-risk start
Personas: store owner, founder or CEO as decision maker, the implementer who installs.

| RTB | Headline | Emotional | Proof to check | Body (25 words max) | CTA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sandbox store | Try it before you install anything | See it work before it touches your store | Open the sandbox before you install anything | Ask the sandbox store for hiking gear the way a shopper would. You see product cards, clarifying questions, and add to cart before installing. | Open the sandbox store |
| Free plan and trial | Start free with 50 conversations a month | See your quota before it runs out | `[IN BUILD]` No surprise charges: Pico pauses before it bills you more | New accounts get a 14 day Growth trial with no card, then move to Free: 50 conversations a month. A quota meter shows usage. | Install free from the Shopify App Store (once live) |
| Four-step setup | Four steps from install to live widget | No theme code to edit | `[IN BUILD]` Read the speed test before you switch it on | Authorize Pico, switch on the Pico Assistant theme embed, sync your catalog, and confirm the widget appears. The checklist tracks each step. | Start the four-step setup |

## Supporting proof points (open proof)
- The Sandbox link in picofinds.com's top menu runs a sample outdoor gear catalog on Pico's real API. Type a request with a price limit, then check the prices on the cards.
- Every card in the sandbox has a View link to the product it came from.
- Try a one-word request such as "boots" in the sandbox, then add a product to the cart. Out-of-stock items cannot be added.
- The Shopper Words Test worksheet lists ten phrases a shopper might use. Try them in the sandbox, then compare them with your own product titles.
- `[IN BUILD]` The plan page states each plan's quota, what counts as one conversation, the alerts at 80% and 100%, and that Pico never charges overage.
- `[IN BUILD]` The technical one-pager publishes Pico's measured Lighthouse difference on Dawn, against a 10-point budget.

## Rules
- Before the listing is live, every App Store CTA reads "Connect your store" and links to picofinds.com.
- Never "sales", "revenue", "conversion", or "ROI" about Pico. Never name a competitor or describe a Shopify tool.
- GCC line, for later only: `gcc-later.md`.


===== prompts/common-tasks.md =====

# Prompt library, common Pico GTM tasks

Filled, runnable prompts for recurring jobs. Each assumes the agent has loaded the router (`CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`). Tools without file access: paste `adapters/portable-control-layer.md` first. Tools with a shell: `python3 tools/brain.py context <task> --audience <a> --format cat` prints the exact load set.

There is no paid ads, cold outbound to store owners, LinkedIn automation, or GCC work in this GTM, so there are no prompts for them. Asked for one, refuse and offer the in-scope channel.

## Merchants

**App Store listing.** "Load `templates/app-store-listing.md`, `reference/app-store-engine.md`, `reference/value-proposition-merchants.md`, and `examples/app-store-listing.md`. Draft or update the Pico AI Shopping Assistant listing, field by field. Shipped capabilities only, per `rules/feature-status.md`. Then run `ops/QA-checklist.md` and list every capability mentioned with its status flag."

**Catalog guide.** "Using `templates/seo-article.md` and `reference/app-store-engine.md`, write a catalog guide for [category] merchants: how shoppers describe [products], and how to name products so they are found. Sample phrases labeled as examples. No industry statistics. End with the Shopper Words Test and the sandbox CTA. QA before returning."

**Comparison page.** "Draft a 'when Pico fits and when it doesn't' page against [option], using `templates/seo-article.md`. Every fact about [option] must be sourced and dated from `reference/competitive-analysis-merchants.md`. Mark any fact older than 30 days for a page-loaded recheck. No disparagement. QA before returning."

**Lifecycle email.** "Write the [email] from `templates/lifecycle-email.md` for a merchant in stage [n], matching `examples/first-insight-email.md`. Only data Pico measures. If its trigger is IN BUILD, say so at the top. QA before returning."

**Review reply.** "Reply to this App Store review using `templates/review-reply.md`: [paste review]. Then give me the signal-log entry and the `review.received` event to add."

## Implementers

**Cold email.** "Using `templates/cold-email.md`, `reference/outreach-engine.md`, and `examples/cold-email-paid-session.md`, write a first email to a [freelancer / agency] who [context]. Under 120 words, CAN-SPAM footer, no partner terms. QA before returning."

**LinkedIn.** "Write a connection note and first message for a [role] at a [segment], from `templates/linkedin-message.md`. Sent by hand. QA before returning."

**Upwork or Fiverr.** "Write the [Upwork job post / Fiverr brief] for the Paid Usability Session from `templates/marketplace-job-post.md`, matching `examples/upwork-job-post.md`. Nothing about the partner program. QA before returning."

**Partner invitation, from week 6.** "Write the partnership invitation for a session participant met by [email / LinkedIn], quoting the terms from `reference/partner-program.md` exactly. Refuse if they were met on Upwork or Fiverr."

## Sales, partners, and strategy

**Call prep.** "Prepare me for a call with a [persona] at a [segment]. Load the matching `reference/icp-personas-*.md`, `reference/objection-handling.md`, and `reference/competitor-battlecards.md`. Give the three objections they will raise and the honest answers."

**Objection.** "Draft a response to '[objection]' for [audience], grounded in `reference/objection-handling.md`. Say not yet where the answer is not yet."

**Strategy question.** "Answer from `context/Pico_GTM_Master_Context.md` and `ops/decisions.md` only: [question]. Cite the decision IDs. If the brain does not settle it, say so and propose an open item."

**Investor or advisor update.** "Write a monthly update from `innovation/LEDGER.md`, `reference/launch-plan.md`, and the newest file in `snapshots/`. Internal numbers are allowed here. No claim that is not in an event."

## The compounding loop

**Log a signal.** "Log this in `ops/signal-log.md`: [paste note]. Keep the verbatim. Classify the type, assign a disposition with the thresholds in that file, add tags, and if it is a PATCH or AMEND, list exactly which files change. Then run `python3 tools/brain.py signal` with the same fields."

**Log an activity.** "Record this as an event: [what happened]. Pick the type from `reference/innovation-accounting.md`, fill `data` and `refs`, and run `python3 tools/brain.py event`."

**Weekly review.** "Run the Monday loop: `python3 tools/brain.py tripwires`, triage new signals, update WATCH counters, then `python3 tools/brain.py ledger`. Report what changed and what did not."

**Snapshot.** "Run `python3 tools/brain.py snapshot [label]`, then fill every section from [data]. Diff section 6 against `rules/feature-status.md` and finish with what this changes, including 'no ledger change this period' if that is the honest answer."

**Amend.** "This changed: [fact]. Follow the AMEND procedure: the `rules/` ledger first, then the master context with a version bump, then a dated `ops/decisions.md` entry with what it does not change, then grep and fix the copy bank, then `python3 tools/brain.py build`."

**Audit.** "Run `python3 tools/brain.py audit`, then produce one real asset using only the brain and QA it. Report anything the brain could not supply."
